# ClearVoting Redesign Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Rebuild clearvoting.org on the "Spine" design so a first-time visitor gets from their ZIP code to their own senators and House member in two taps, sees each member's dated record on the first screen, and never reads anything the data does not support, merged before Election Day (merge-by Monday 2026-10-13).

**Architecture:** The FastAPI server renders the first blocks of every page into the existing static HTML shells: a `<!--content-->` marker, one escape helper `h()`, and pure formatters in a new `app/render.py`. It reads only data loaded at startup, plus two new sync-built derived files (`votes_index.json`, `state_overview/*.json`) and two sanctioned public-data files (the ZIP crosswalk and the Senate 2026 seats list). One fresh `static/css/site.css` and one shared `static/js/site.js` replace `styles.css`, `broadsheet.css` and `viz.js`, and the page scripts become thin enhancers that build DOM with `el()`/`textContent` only.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3 / FastAPI / uvicorn, stdlib `html` and `zoneinfo`, pytest; vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no framework and no build step; flat JSON in `data/synced/`; Render auto-deploy from `main`, with Cloudflare in front; out-of-repo Node + Playwright scripts (`~/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/shots/`) for browser gates only; Pillow in the dev/sync context for og cards only.

## Global Constraints

- Stack: FastAPI + vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, flat JSON in data/synced, no framework, no build step, no database, no template engine; one PR on branch redesign/2026-09 that Joseph merges (spec §2.2 #1).
- Merge-by Monday 2026-10-13; checkpoint 2026-10-06; cut-first order when behind: og Phase B → in-place record pagination → print block → sticky strip → desktop fact strip → og Phase A (spec §10.3).
- Every shell (index, state, member, bill, about, methodology, privacy, 404) keeps a literal <title>…</title> and </head>; the server owns the title via _inject_meta; no client script writes document.title (all three existing writes in bill.js:75, member.js:61, state.js:84 are deleted).
- CSP: script-src 'self' (no inline <script>, no inline on* handlers); img-src 'self' https://www.congress.gov; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (server style= on tally segments is allowed); after fonts land: font-src 'self' and no fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com anywhere.
- No new innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML anywhere; bill.js sanitizeHtml/SAFE_TAGS block stays verbatim (now fed the official_summary field). JS builds DOM with el()/textContent only.
- feedback.js hooks stay: #feedback-modal, #feedback-open, #feedback-cancel, #feedback-overlay, #feedback-form, #feedback-message, #feedback-submit, #feedback-status, #feedback-context, .state-header h1, #data-freshness, #about-feedback-cta. The only structural change: .member-header h2 → .member-header h1 and .bill-header h2 → .bill-header h1, with both feedback.js selectors changed in the same commit (group 2).
- Real data only: fields from data/synced/ plus exactly two new sanctioned files data/synced/zip_districts.json and data/synced/senate_2026.json (each with a _source object and an entry in data/SOURCES.md); derived files only votes_index.json and state_overview/{CA,FL,NY,TX}.json. senate_2026.json _source.method (contains party letters) is never rendered.
- No URL-shape changes and no 301 work: canonical forms are /, /state?code=XX (upper), /member?id=X (upper), /bill?congress=N&type=xx&number=N (lower type), /about, /methodology, /privacy; district/zip/page/topic/position/plain are additive non-canonical params stripped from canonical and Share.
- Party labels never in any default HTML or /api/* payload (party, partyName, partyCode, [R-AL-6] fullName suffix, roll-call members[].party, Speaker candidate names); reveal only via ?show_party=true, remembered only in sessionStorage['cv-show-party']; site.js removes legacy localStorage['cv-show-party'] once.
- Storage: localStorage['cv-home'] = {state, district, savedAt}, written only on #mine landing, the 'Remember District N as mine' tap, or an in-place bill-page ZIP pick; no cookies; history.replaceState only for browse ?q=, removing #mine, and cut-first in-place pagination; no pushState.
- No scores, grades, rankings, stance labels, ratios or percentages on list rows; no 'leans'/'mostly in favor'/'fights for'/'N of M'; never the words 'blocked', 'let the veto stand', 'taken up'; no string matching case-sensitive \b(On|Not on) the ballot in app/render.py, shells or site.js — ballot copy describes the SEAT ('This seat is on the ballot Nov 3, 2026', 'Seat up Nov 3', 'Special election Nov 3', 'Special election for this seat Nov 3, 2026').
- Withheld/absent summaries: displayable_summary(bill_id) = summary exists and needs_review is not true; the ~115 needs_review summaries are shown exactly like the 60 unsummarized bills (official title in Lora 500 + 'No plain-English summary yet' seal); counts are computed from data, never hard-coded (the '115 bills with no decisive vote' figure is approximate — tests assert against the real question-class table).
- Member narratives withdrawn: /api/members/{id}/summary deleted (group 6); /methodology#ai says 'Member summaries are withdrawn until they can be rewritten without stance labels.' AI arguments module removed from pages and /ai-summary (returns only one_liner and provisions; 404 {"available": false} when missing or needs_review).
- Recent votes = the eight most recent decisive (class D) votes on bills with a displayable summary and non-empty policy_area, Yea/Aye→yes, Nay/No→no, dedupe per bill_id newest first (mark seen only on pick), round-robin by policy area, output newest first — regardless of the member's position.
- About names the maintainer 'Joseph Garcia, an independent volunteer'; the only contact is the feedback form; no email address is published anywhere.
- Campaign money: one dated 2024-cycle sentence with https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/{fec_candidate_id}/ only when totals has total_receipts, total_individual, total_pac, total_disbursements and fec_candidate_id exists; otherwise the meta line 'Campaign finance isn't in our data for this member yet.'
- No Render plan change; cold start handled only by edge-cacheable headers (Cloudflare Cache Rule is Joseph's ops step, §12.4).
- Commit atomicity (§10.3): a page's shell, JS, render blocks and switch to static/css/site.css land in ONE commit; commit 1 is additive only — no field/endpoint an old page reads is removed or reshaped before its consumer's rewrite commit; every task leaves the site deployable and pytest green (baseline 370 tests; run /Users/josephgarcia/Claude/Projects/Non-Profit/ClearVote/.venv/bin/python -m pytest from the worktree).
- Server rendering: _serve_html(filename, meta, content_html) replaces a literal <!--content--> inside <main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">; every interpolated value passes through app/render.py h() (html.escape(str(x), quote=True)); URLs only from validated ids + urllib.parse.quote; SSR page routes are plain def; render path reads only startup-loaded data plus one member_votes file per member page and at most two roll-call files per bill page.
- Visual system: tokens in one :root of static/css/site.css (values exactly §6.1: --paper #F5F6FA, --card #FFFFFF, --ink #1B1B1B, --ink-soft #5B616B, --ink-meta #5F656D, --navy #112E51, --blue #0071BC, --blue-dim #205493, --yes #2E7D3A, --yes-text #1F5E2D, --yes-tint #DDE7E3, --no #B3261E, --no-text #8E1B21, --no-tint #EDDDE0, --error #8A1C1C, --rule #D6D7D9, --rule-soft #E8E8E8, --tap 44px, radii 4px/8px); font-size only var(--t-*) tokens (§6.2); spacing --s1..--s16 4px scale; exactly two breakpoints 560 and 880 declared once at the end; box-shadow only on .state-link and .vote-card; red only in the vote component; JS applies classes, never colours.
- Definition-of-done gates (§6.9): scrollWidth <= innerWidth at 320/375/768/1280; no text under 12px; every text token >= 4.5:1 on --paper and --card; standalone controls >= 44x44; no content defaulting to opacity:0; nothing floating over the primary action on phones (no floating feedback button under 880); fold checks at 375x812; TTFB < 300 ms local warm; browser gates run from out-of-repo ~/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/shots/gates.mjs, never in pytest/CI.
- Cache-Control (§9.5): 5xx and 4xx-except-404 → no-store; 404 → public, max-age=60; /static/* 200 → public, max-age=31536000, immutable with ?v= from RENDER_GIT_COMMIT[:12] or a static file-list+mtime hash; /static/og/* → public, max-age=86400; HTML 200 → public, max-age=0, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=3600; /state?zip= 302 → public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400; GET /api/* 200 → public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400; /api/health, POST /api/notify, /api/feedback → no-store.
- Dates: one helper (long 'September 3, 2026' in sentences, short 'Sep 3, 2026' in meta); Election Day countdown in America/Los_Angeles via zoneinfo ('Election Day is today' on Nov 3 Pacific, omitted from Nov 4).
- June 2026 plan constraints still bind (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-inner-page-broadsheet.md): keep ?v=N asset links, wire back-links via addEventListener, names humanized everywhere via display_name/displayName, vote colours always paired with text.
- Planning/build agents do not use Playwright/browser MCP tools interactively; browser checks run only through the out-of-repo gates.mjs/shoot.mjs scripts; the QA-walkthrough keyboard/screen-reader pass is scripted, code/curl-first.

## Overview

**Current behaviour (baseline commit `712c5b4`, frontend identical to the live site):**
- `app/main.py:85-91` `_serve_html` reads a static shell, rewrites `?v=`, runs `_inject_meta` (`app/main.py:58`), and sends `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` on every page. No page content is server-rendered: `/member`, `/bill`, `/state` (`app/main.py:239-262`) return empty shells, and JS fills them after load.
- Three scripts overwrite the server's title: `static/js/bill.js:75`, `static/js/member.js:61`, `static/js/state.js:84`.
- The CSP allows `https://fonts.googleapis.com` in `style-src` (`app/main.py:110`), and every shell loads Google Fonts (`static/index.html:8-10`). This makes the "no third-party requests" privacy claim false.
- Latest vote and bill-vote lookups scan every roll-call file at request time: `app/services/data_service.py:242-256` (`_build_latest_vote`) and `:333-345` (`_build_bill_votes_index`). `/api/members/{state}/overview` (`app/routers/members.py:102-154`) aggregates participation rates per request, and the home roster uses `include_stats` (`app/routers/members.py:164-202`, `static/js/app.js:250`).
- The member page shows an AI narrative with stance labels (`static/js/member.js:458`, `:536-538`, fed by `/api/members/{id}/summary`, `app/routers/members.py:72-91`). The bill page shows the AI "both-sides arguments" module (`static/js/bill.js:265-268`).
- `static/js/feedback.js:21` and `:30` hook `.member-header h2` / `.bill-header h2`. `:180` overwrites `#data-freshness` from `/api/health`, and `:195-196` runs an IntersectionObserver entrance animation. Home says "Updated weekly" (`static/index.html:66`) although the AI sync has been dormant since 2026-07-07.
- There is no ZIP lookup: visitors pick a state, then find their district by hand. The rate limiter keys on the proxy address (`app/limiter.py:4`), so limits are global. Notify logs the subscriber's email (`app/routers/notify.py:70`).
- The styles are `static/css/styles.css` (3,848 lines, about 36 % dead) plus `static/css/broadsheet.css` (455 lines), and the charts live in `static/js/viz.js` (291 lines).

**New behaviour (spec §1):**
- **Home:** the ZIP field ("Where do you live?") on the first screen. Then a server-rendered lead, the Latest Vote card (its "The latest vote" is an `<h2 class="kicker">`), and the Record, ordered newest-by-activity whether or not a bill has a summary. A dated edition line replaces "Updated weekly".
- **ZIP path:** `GET /state?zip=11570` resolves through `/api/districts/{zip}` logic and returns a single 302 to `/state?code=NY&district=4#mine`. Split and partial ZIPs 302 to `code`+`zip` and show a picker, and unknown ZIPs render an honest not-found state with the house.gov fallback. `cv-home` is written only on the reader's own act, and `#mine` is removed with `replaceState`.
- **Delegation:** senators first, then the House by district. Each row shows one dated decisive vote. The seat seal describes the seat, never the person.
- **Member:** h1 header with scoped counts, then "Recent votes" (the eight most recent decisive votes, regardless of position), then the Record grouped by bill with server pagination and GET filters, then sponsored bills and one dated 2024-cycle money sentence with an FEC link. No narrative, no charts.
- **Bill:** h1 one-liner (or a capped official title), an outcome sentence, a "How did your representatives vote?" slot filled from storage or an in-place ZIP lookup, roll-call tables with `<caption>`/`scope`, a fact box, and a plain-text official first paragraph. No arguments module.
- **Trust pages:** About (names Joseph Garcia; contact through the feedback form only), Methodology & Corrections (server-filled counts), Privacy (matches the code), and a real 404.
- **Reach:** server-only titles and canonical links, real 404 statuses, per-URL sitemap `lastmod`, Cache-Control by status and route (§9.5), self-hosted fonts with a CSP of `font-src 'self'`, a stable `?v=`, and four static og cards (cut-first).

## Design Decisions

- **Member narratives are withdrawn (Joseph, confirmed 2026-09-22, spec §2.5 A).** `/api/members/{id}/summary` is deleted in the member commit (T6.3), and `/methodology#ai` says "Member summaries are withdrawn until they can be rewritten without stance labels." Rationale: 34 of 150 narratives contain "lean(s)" and 11 contain stance ratios, which break the no-characterization rule (§2.2 #9). Regenerating them is out of scope, and withdrawing them can be reversed later.
- **"Key votes (4 yes + 4 no)" becomes "Recent votes" (Joseph, confirmed, §2.5 B).** The picker takes the eight most recent decisive votes on bills with a displayable summary, one per topic where possible, whatever the member's position. Rationale: choosing by position manufactures an even-looking profile, and "key" implies an importance judgement the rule does not make.
- **The 115 `needs_review` summaries are withheld (Joseph, confirmed, §2.5 C).** `displayable_summary(bill_id)` is the single gate on every surface. Withheld bills look exactly like unsummarized ones (official title plus the "No plain-English summary yet" seal) and are counted on `/methodology`. Rationale: they failed the automated grader.
- **Merge-by Monday 2026-10-13, checkpoint 2026-10-06, cut-first order (Joseph, confirmed, §10.3).** The phases follow the spec's commit order. The minimum shippable scope is Phases 1–7 plus T8.1–T8.3, Phase 9 and Phase 11. The cut-first tasks (T10.1 og Phase B → T10.2 in-place pagination → T10.3 print → T10.4 sticky strip → T10.5 desktop fact strip → T8.4 og Phase A) are each additive, so dropping any of them breaks nothing. Rationale: server-rendered pages need crawl and share time before November 3.
- **Commit 1 is additive only.** No field or endpoint an old page reads is removed or reshaped until the commit that rewrites its consumer. `include_stats` goes with home (T3.3), the overview reshape with delegation (T4.2), `/summary` and the member trims with the member page (T6.3), and the `/ai-summary`/sponsor/roll-call party trims with the bill page (T7.4). Rationale: every commit leaves the live site working.
- **Notify state validation moves to the home switch (T3.3), not commit 1.** This is a recorded deviation from the letter of §10 #16: the old home form posts `''` or a covered state, so enforcing the rule earlier would break the live form. T1.10 lands only the email-logging fix.
- **One escape helper plus a hostile-input registry test, not a template engine (§2.5 decline 3).** Every interpolated value passes through `render.h()`, and the test feeds `<script>`, `"><img>`, entities and `javascript:` through every renderer.
- **Sync-time indexes, not request-time scans (§10 #3, #7).** `votes_index.json` and `state_overview/*.json` are built by new `sync.py` steps, committed in this PR, and regenerated by the weekly workflow. The runtime does dict lookups and at most two roll-call file reads per bill page.
- **The two sanctioned data files are copied, not re-derived.** `zip_districts.json` is rebuilt by the moved `scripts/build_zip_crosswalk.py`, whose only change is writing the `_source` block. `senate_2026.json` (Cornyn TX class 2 regular; Moody FL class 3 special; `class` an integer; retrieved 2026-09-19) is copied unchanged.
- **Counts are computed, never hard-coded.** "115 bills with no decisive vote" (§7.1) is approximate; T1.2 measured 113 with the spec table. Tests assert against the real question-class table, never a literal 115.
- **The Latest Vote card's "The latest vote" is an `<h2 class="kicker">`.** One markup satisfies both §4.1 m3 and the §8 item 2 heading outline (T3.2).
- **After a ZIP submit, `cv-home` is written and `#mine` removed, including when the 302 comes from the edge cache.** The 302 carries the fragment in `Location`, and the browser acts on it client-side, so a cached 302 behaves the same. A scripted QA step (T11.3) proves this.
- **Ballot copy describes the seat, never the person** (PM decision, §7.4): "This seat is on the ballot Nov 3, 2026". The data does not say whether a member is running. A grep gate forbids `\b(On|Not on) the ballot` in render code, shells and `site.js`.
- **Resolved PM decisions (§12.3):** About names "Joseph Garcia, an independent volunteer", and the feedback form is the only contact, with no email address anywhere. No Render plan change: cold start is deferred to ops, and this PR only adds edge-cacheable headers. The AI "supporters say / critics say" module is removed from pages and APIs. Campaign money is one dated 2024-cycle sentence with an FEC link, only for members with complete totals.
- **Browser checks stay out of CI.** The §6.9 gates run from `~/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/shots/gates.mjs`, text-first with capped screenshots, never in pytest (tests.yml has no node).

```python
"""The two sanctioned data files (spec §2.2 #6, §5.1, §10 #1-#2) and the invariants
of the real-data fixture slices every later test relies on (§10 #22)."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
SYNCED = ROOT / "data" / "synced"
FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "synced"
COVERED = {"CA", "FL", "NY", "TX"}
FIXTURE_ZIPS = {"10001", "11201", "11570", "73949", "88430", "89019", "97635"}


def _load(path: Path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


# --- Sanctioned files: provenance ---

@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["zip_districts.json", "senate_2026.json"])
def test_sanctioned_file_has_source(name):
    source = _load(SYNCED / name)["_source"]
    assert source["url"].startswith("https://")
    assert re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", source["retrieved"])
    assert source["name"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["zip_districts.json", "senate_2026.json"])
def test_sanctioned_file_listed_in_sources_md(name):
    sources_md = (ROOT / "data" / "SOURCES.md").read_text()
    source = _load(SYNCED / name)["_source"]
    assert f"data/synced/{name}" in sources_md
    assert source["retrieved"] in sources_md


# --- Crosswalk ---

def test_crosswalk_shape():
    data = _load(SYNCED / "zip_districts.json")
    # Loaders skip every "_" key; _source is the only one.
    assert [k for k in data if k.startswith("_")] == ["_source"]
    zips = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
    assert len(zips) == 6639
    for zip_code, districts in zips.items():
        assert re.fullmatch(r"\d{5}", zip_code)
        assert districts, zip_code
        shares = [d["share"] for d in districts]
        assert shares == sorted(shares, reverse=True), zip_code
        for d in districts:
            assert d["state"] in COVERED
            assert isinstance(d["district"], int) and d["district"] >= 1
            assert 0 < d["share"] <= 1


def test_crosswalk_source_describes_land_area_share():
    source = _load(SYNCED / "zip_districts.json")["_source"]
    assert source["retrieved"] == "2026-09-11"
    assert source["url"] == "https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/cd-sld/"
    assert "land area" in source["share"]
    assert "17 U.S.C." in source["licence"]


def test_crosswalk_known_zips():
    data = _load(SYNCED / "zip_districts.json")
    assert data["11570"] == [{"district": 4, "share": 1.0, "state": "NY"}]
    assert [(d["state"], d["district"]) for d in data["11201"]] == [("NY", 10), ("NY", 7)]
    assert data["73949"] == [{"district": 13, "share": 0.1367, "state": "TX"}]


# --- Senate seats up in 2026 ---

def test_senate_2026_seats():
    data = _load(SYNCED / "senate_2026.json")
    assert data["election_day"] == "2026-11-03"
    seats = {s["bioguideId"]: s for s in data["seats"]}
    assert set(seats) == {"C001056", "M001244"}
    assert seats["C001056"]["kind"] == "regular" and seats["C001056"]["state"] == "TX"
    assert seats["M001244"]["kind"] == "special" and seats["M001244"]["state"] == "FL"
    for seat in data["seats"]:
        assert type(seat["class"]) is int and seat["class"] in (1, 2, 3)


def test_senate_2026_seats_are_real_members():
    members = {m["bioguideId"] for m in _load(SYNCED / "members.json")["members"]}
    for seat in _load(SYNCED / "senate_2026.json")["seats"]:
        assert seat["bioguideId"] in members


# --- Fixture slices (§10 #22) ---

def test_fixture_sanctioned_files_mirror_real_ones():
    real = _load(SYNCED / "zip_districts.json")
    fixture = _load(FIXTURES / "zip_districts.json")
    assert fixture["_source"] == real["_source"]
    assert set(fixture) - {"_source"} == FIXTURE_ZIPS
    for zip_code in FIXTURE_ZIPS:
        assert fixture[zip_code] == real[zip_code]
    assert _load(FIXTURES / "senate_2026.json") == _load(SYNCED / "senate_2026.json")


def test_fixture_member_votes_are_whole_real_files():
```

```python
"""Build zip_districts.json from the Census 2020 ZCTA <-> 119th Congressional District relationship files.
Source: https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/cd-sld/tab20_cd11920_zcta520_st{FIPS}.txt (public domain, 17 U.S.C. 105).
Share = land-area overlap (AREALAND_PART / AREALAND_ZCTA5_20); the files carry no population share. Slivers under 1% are dropped.
Usage: python scripts/build_zip_crosswalk.py <raw_dir> data/synced/zip_districts.json"""
import csv, io, json, sys, collections, pathlib
RAW = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); OUT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
STATES = {"06": "CA", "12": "FL", "36": "NY", "48": "TX"}
EXPECTED_CDS = {"CA": 52, "FL": 28, "NY": 26, "TX": 38}
# Written into the file as "_source" (spec §5.1). "retrieved" is the date the four
# raw files were downloaded; change it only when they are downloaded again.
SOURCE = {
    "name": "U.S. Census Bureau 2020 ZCTA to 119th Congressional District relationship files",
    "url": "https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/cd-sld/",
    "retrieved": "2026-09-11",
    "licence": "Public domain (17 U.S.C. §105)",
    "share": "land area (AREALAND_PART / AREALAND_ZCTA5_20), covered states only",
}
by_zip = collections.defaultdict(list)
for fips, st in STATES.items():
    text = (RAW / f"tab20_cd11920_zcta520_st{fips}.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter="|"))
    cols = rows[0].keys()
    need = ["GEOID_CD119_20", "GEOID_ZCTA5_20", "AREALAND_PART", "AREALAND_ZCTA5_20"]
    missing = [c for c in need if c not in cols]
    if missing: sys.exit(f"{st}: missing columns {missing}; have {list(cols)}")
    cds = set(); n = 0
    for r in rows:
        z = r["GEOID_ZCTA5_20"].strip(); cd = r["GEOID_CD119_20"].strip()
        if not z or len(cd) != 4 or cd[:2] != fips: continue
        try: part = float(r["AREALAND_PART"] or 0); tot = float(r["AREALAND_ZCTA5_20"] or 0)
        except ValueError: continue
        share = part / tot if tot > 0 else 0.0
        d = int(cd[2:]); cds.add(d)
        by_zip[z].append({"state": st, "district": d, "share": round(share, 4)}); n += 1
    print(f"{st}: {n} rows, {len(cds)} districts (expected {EXPECTED_CDS[st]})")
    if len(cds) != EXPECTED_CDS[st]: sys.exit(f"{st}: district count mismatch — wrong vintage?")
final = {}
for z, lst in by_zip.items():
    kept = [e for e in lst if e["share"] >= 0.01] or lst
    kept.sort(key=lambda e: -e["share"])
    final[z] = kept
OUT.write_text(json.dumps({"_source": SOURCE, **final}, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True))
one = sum(1 for v in final.values() if len(v) == 1)
print(f"zips {len(final)}, single-district {one} ({one/len(final):.0%}), bytes {OUT.stat().st_size}")
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write `data/SOURCES.md`.**

```markdown
# Data sources for the two sanctioned files

Everything else in `data/synced/` comes from the Congress.gov API, Senate.gov and
House Clerk roll-call XML, and the FEC API through `sync.py`. These two files are
the only data the redesign adds from outside that sync (spec §2.2 #6). Each also
carries the same facts in its own `_source` object.

## data/synced/zip_districts.json

- **What:** ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA) → 119th Congress district, for California,
  Florida, New York and Texas only. 6,639 ZCTAs; each lists its districts with the
  share of the ZCTA's land area inside each one, largest first. Slivers under 1 % are dropped.
- **Source:** U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 ZCTA to 119th Congressional District relationship
  files `tab20_cd11920_zcta520_st06.txt`, `…_st12.txt`, `…_st36.txt`, `…_st48.txt`,
  https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/cd-sld/
- **Licence:** Public domain (U.S. government work, 17 U.S.C. §105).
- **Retrieved:** 2026-09-11.
- **Share:** land area (`AREALAND_PART / AREALAND_ZCTA5_20`). The files carry no population share.
- **Build:** download the four files into a folder, then run
  `python scripts/build_zip_crosswalk.py <folder> data/synced/zip_districts.json`.
  The script checks each state's district count (CA 52, FL 28, NY 26, TX 38) and
  writes the `_source` object. Update `SOURCE["retrieved"]` in the script when the
  files are downloaded again.

## data/synced/senate_2026.json

- **What:** the senators from the four covered states whose seats are on the
  November 3, 2026 ballot: John Cornyn (TX, Class II, regular election) and
  Ashley Moody (FL, Class III, special election for an appointed seat).
  House seats are all on the ballot by definition and are not listed.
- **Source:** U.S. Senate, "Senators by class":
  https://www.senate.gov/senators/Class_II.htm and https://www.senate.gov/senators/Class_III.htm
- **Licence:** Public domain (U.S. government work, 17 U.S.C. §105).
- **Retrieved:** 2026-09-19.
- **Build:** by hand from the two pages (two rows); no script. `class` is an integer.
  `_source.method` records how the rows were read and is never rendered on the site.
```

```bash
"""One-off: cut real-data fixture slices into tests/fixtures/synced (plan T1.1).
Run from the repo root. Deterministic: re-running rewrites the same bytes."""
import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

REAL = Path("data/synced")
FIX = Path("tests/fixtures/synced")
COVERED = {"CA", "FL", "NY", "TX"}


def dump(path: Path, obj) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=False) + "\n")


# 1. Roll calls: real files, members[] trimmed to the four covered states
#    (the only rows the index tallies and the covered relation read); every
#    other field, including counts, is byte-for-byte the real value.
ROLL_CALLS = {
    "house": [
        "117_1_00006",  # On Ordering the Previous Question, H.Res. 8 (117th; G000602 not yet seated)
        "118_1_00037",  # H.R. 21 amendment (Failed)
        "118_1_00041",  # H.R. 21 amendment (Agreed to)
        "118_1_00093",  # H.R. 21 On Passage (Passed)
        "119_1_00002",  # Election of the Speaker (candidate-name positions)
        "119_2_00295",  # H.R. 4795 On Passage 237-169, the real latest roll call
    ],
    "senate": [
        "119_1_00632", "119_1_00645", "119_1_00648", "119_1_00654",
        "119_2_00001",  # On the Nomination PN12-1 (index only, never in records)
        "119_2_00011",
        "119_2_00020",  # H.R. 7148 On Passage; its AI summary is needs_review
        "119_2_00037", "119_2_00084", "119_2_00105", "119_2_00163",
        "119_2_00182", "119_2_00184",
        "119_2_00223",  # amendment S.Amdt. 6715 to S.Amdt. 6711 to H.R. 5334 (bill_id null; parent 119-hr-5334)
        "119_2_00224",  # H.R. 5334 On Passage of the Bill
        "119_2_00228",  # H.R. 6500 On Passage of the Bill 90-6 (3/5)
        "119_2_00231",  # Cloture on the Motion to Proceed S. 5271, rejected 52-46 (newest S000148 row, class P)
    ],
}
for chamber, keys in ROLL_CALLS.items():
    for key in keys:
        vote = json.loads((REAL / "votes" / chamber / f"{key}.json").read_text())
        vote["members"] = [m for m in vote.get("members", []) if m.get("state") in COVERED]
        dump(FIX / "votes" / chamber / f"{key}.json", vote)

# 2. Member vote files: copied whole (S000148: 1,061 rows, 478 with bill_id null).
for member_id in ("S000148", "G000602"):
    shutil.copyfile(REAL / "member_votes" / f"{member_id}.json", FIX / "member_votes" / f"{member_id}.json")

# 3. Members: synthetic S001217 and D000032 stay (with their directOrderName until
#    T1.3); S000148 is replaced by its real record; four real records are added:
#    NY senator G000555 (ZIP senator_ids), NY-4 G000602, NY-18 R000579 (empty donation
#    totals) and TX C001056 (the "regular" seat in senate_2026.json). Moody (M001244)
#    is left out so the Florida roster tests keep their two members.
real_members = {m["bioguideId"]: m for m in json.loads((REAL / "members.json").read_text())["members"]}
fixture_members = json.loads((FIX / "members.json").read_text())["members"]
members = [m for m in fixture_members if m["bioguideId"] in ("S001217", "D000032")]
members += [real_members[i] for i in ("S000148", "G000555", "G000602", "R000579", "C001056")]
dump(FIX / "members.json", {"members": members})

# 4. Bills: the three synthetic bills stay; every bill a new roll call points at is
#    added verbatim; plus one synthetic hostile-title bill with no roll call.
BILLS = [
    "117-hres-8", "118-hr-21", "119-hr-4795", "119-s-5271", "119-hr-5334", "119-hr-7148",
    "119-hr-6500", "119-hconres-86", "119-hr-6644", "119-s-2", "119-sconres-33", "119-hjres-140",
    "119-hjres-142", "119-hr-6938", "119-sjres-82", "119-s-1071", "119-sres-532", "119-hjres-131",
]
real_bills = {
    f"{b['congress']}-{b['type'].lower()}-{b['number']}": b
    for b in json.loads((REAL / "bills.json").read_text())["bills"]
}
bills = json.loads((FIX / "bills.json").read_text())["bills"][:3]
bills += [real_bills[k] for k in BILLS]
bills.append({
    "congress": 119,
    "type": "HR",
    "number": "99999",
    "title": "Synthetic <b>bold</b> & \"quoted\" 'apostrophe' title for escaping tests",
    "introducedDate": "2025-01-10",
    "latestAction": {"actionDate": "2025-01-15", "text": "Referred to committee."},
    "sponsors": [],
    "policyArea": {"name": "Government Operations and Politics"},
    "summaries": [],
})
dump(FIX / "bills.json", {"bills": bills})

# 5. AI summaries: the synthetic 119-hr-1 entry stays; real entries for the added
#    bills (most carry `arguments`; 119-hr-7148 carries needs_review: true).
real_ai = json.loads((REAL / "ai_summaries.json").read_text())
ai = json.loads((FIX / "ai_summaries.json").read_text())
for key in BILLS:
    if key in real_ai:
        ai[key] = real_ai[key]
dump(FIX / "ai_summaries.json", ai)

# 6. Donations: complete (S000148), complete-but-tiny (G000602), empty totals
#    (R000579); every other fixture member is missing.
real_donations = json.loads((REAL / "donations.json").read_text())
dump(FIX / "donations.json", {k: real_donations[k] for k in ("S000148", "G000602", "R000579")})

# 7. Sync metadata: seeded ai_summaries_updated (spec §7.4).
metadata = json.loads((FIX / "sync_metadata.json").read_text())
metadata["ai_summaries_updated"] = "2026-07-07"
dump(FIX / "sync_metadata.json", metadata)

# 8. Sanctioned files: crosswalk subset with its _source, and the Senate seats file.
crosswalk = json.loads((REAL / "zip_districts.json").read_text())
subset = {"_source": crosswalk["_source"]}
for zip_code in ("10001", "11201", "11570", "73949", "88430", "89019", "97635"):
    subset[zip_code] = crosswalk[zip_code]
dump(FIX / "zip_districts.json", subset)
shutil.copyfile(REAL / "senate_2026.json", FIX / "senate_2026.json")
print("fixtures written")
EOF
```

- Consumes: T1.1 fixtures `tests/fixtures/synced/votes/senate/119_2_00231.json` and `votes/house/119_2_00295.json`; real `data/synced/votes/*/*.json` and `data/synced/bills.json` (the real-data test skips when absent); `app.services.data_service.DataService._parse_bill_document` and `_parse_vote_date` (existing, used only by the real-data test).
- Produces (`app/render.py`); `rc` below is one `votes_index.json` `roll_calls` entry — the formatters read `question`, `plain`, `class`, `result`, `counts` {yeas, nays, present, absent}, `date` (ISO), `threshold` and `bill`, and fall back to classifying `question` when `plain`/`class` are absent; `chamber` is `"House"` or `"Senate"` (lower case and "House of Representatives" are accepted):
  - `QUESTION_CLASSES: list[dict]` — the §7.1 table in match order; each row `{"id": str, "class": "D"|"P", "plain": str, "noun": str | None, "threshold": "2/3" | None, "pattern": re.Pattern}` compiled with `re.IGNORECASE`, JS-portable (site.js mirrors a row as `{pattern: row["pattern"].pattern, flags: "i", plain, noun, class}`). `PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK` is the "any other question string" row (not in the list).
  - `classify(question: str | None) -> dict` (the row), `question_class(question: str | None) -> "D" | "P"`, `plain_question(question: str | None) -> str`.
  - `parse_threshold(result: str | None, plain: str | None = None, question: str | None = None) -> "2/3" | "3/5" | None` (the index's `threshold` field; sync.py calls this one function, there is no second threshold parser). A question naming "Suspend the Rules", "Objections of the President", "Overriding the Veto" or starting "On the Veto" implies two-thirds, the same rule as site.js `twoThirdsNeeded` (G2), so a suspension-concur row, which has no threshold of its own, still reads "2/3".
  - `format_date(value: str | None, short: bool | str = False) -> str` — "September 3, 2026" / "Sep 3, 2026"; also accepts the style strings `"short"`/`"long"`. (It lands here rather than in T1.3 because `outcome_sentence` needs it; T1.3 consumes it.)
  - `result_phrase(rc: dict, chamber: str) -> str` — the §7.2 seal text ("Passed the House 237–169", "Debate not ended 52–46 (60 needed)", "Speaker elected", …).
  - `outcome_sentence(rc: dict, chamber: str) -> str | None` — the §7.3 sentence; `None` for Speaker elections and nominations.
  - `bill_status(laws: list | None, latest_by_chamber: dict | None, bill_type: str | None = None) -> {"text": str, "variant": "final" | "moving"}` — `latest_by_chamber` maps `"House"`/`"Senate"` (any case) to that chamber's newest class-D `rc` or `None`; simple resolutions are recognised from `bill_type` or `rc["bill"]`.
  - `position_chip(vote: str | None) -> {"text", "variant", "short"}` — `variant` is the `.chip--{variant}` suffix (`yes`, `no`, `nv`, `present`, `other`).

**Resolves:** spec §7.1 (question classes, positions), §7.2 (seal text, thresholds, ties, bill status seal; no "blocked", "let the veto stand", "taken up"), §7.3 (outcome sentences, one date helper), §10 #12 (Python formatters). Findings F11 (one vocabulary), F27 (result vocabulary by question class, explicit Amendment/Motion/Speaker labels), F32 (derived status seal from decisive votes; one date helper).

Decisions recorded here (plain language): the table follows the spec rows in order, with three readings the spec's "[…]" and "parentheticals are read" allow — "On Concurring in …" counts as accepting the other chamber's changes, and "On the Motion (… Motion to Commit/Proceed/Discharge …)" is read by its parenthetical. With this table 113 real bills have no decisive vote (the spec's "115" is approximate; the test asserts against the table, never a fixed number). A rejected vote that needed a supermajority says so ("(60 needed)" / "(two-thirds needed)" in seals, "; two-thirds were needed" in sentences), so a 52–47 "rejected" never reads as a contradiction.

```python
"""Unit tests for the pure formatters in app/render.py (spec §7.1-§7.5)."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from app import render
from app.render import (
    QUESTION_CLASSES,
    bill_status,
    format_date,
    outcome_sentence,
    parse_threshold,
    plain_question,
    position_chip,
    question_class,
    result_phrase,
)

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "synced"
REAL_VOTES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "data" / "synced" / "votes"
FORBIDDEN = ("blocked", "let the veto stand", "taken up")


def _rc(question, result, counts, iso_date="2026-09-03"):
    """A votes_index.json roll_calls entry (the fields the formatters read)."""
    return {"question": question, "plain": plain_question(question), "class": question_class(question),
            "result": result, "counts": counts, "date": iso_date, "threshold": None}


def _phrase(question, result, counts, chamber="House"):
    return result_phrase(_rc(question, result, counts), chamber)


def _sentence(question, result, counts, chamber, iso_date):
    return outcome_sentence(_rc(question, result, counts, iso_date), chamber)


# --- §7.1 question classes: every table row, real question strings ---

def test_question_class_table(question, cls, plain):
    assert question_class(question) == cls
    assert plain_question(question) == plain


def test_question_classes_are_js_mirrorable():
    # site.js builds new RegExp(row.pattern, "i") from these; no Python-only syntax.
    for row in QUESTION_CLASSES:
        source = row["pattern"].pattern
        for python_only in ("(?P<", "(?P=", "(?<", "\\A", "\\Z", "(?i", "(?x"):
            assert python_only not in source, source
        assert row["pattern"].flags & re.IGNORECASE
        assert row["class"] in ("D", "P")
    assert len({row["plain"] for row in QUESTION_CLASSES}) == len(QUESTION_CLASSES)


def test_question_class_over_fixture_roll_calls():
    for path in sorted((FIXTURES / "votes").glob("*/*.json")):
        vote = json.loads(path.read_text())
        assert question_class(vote.get("question")) in ("D", "P"), path.name
    rc = json.loads((FIXTURES / "votes" / "senate" / "119_2_00231.json").read_text())
    assert question_class(rc["question"]) == "P"
    rc = json.loads((FIXTURES / "votes" / "house" / "119_2_00295.json").read_text())
    assert question_class(rc["question"]) == "D"


@pytest.mark.skipif(not REAL_VOTES.exists(), reason="real data/synced/votes not present")
def test_every_real_bill_with_a_decisive_vote_gets_a_status_seal():
    from app.services.data_service import DataService, _parse_vote_date

    bills = {
        f"{b['congress']}-{b['type'].lower()}-{b['number']}": b
        for b in json.loads((REAL_VOTES.parent / "bills.json").read_text())["bills"]
    }
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    outputs = []
    for path in REAL_VOTES.glob("*/*.json"):
        vote = json.loads(path.read_text())
        chamber = "Senate" if path.parent.name == "senate" else "House"
        rc = _rc(vote.get("question"), vote.get("result"), vote.get("counts"))
        outputs.append(result_phrase(rc, chamber))
        outputs.append(outcome_sentence(rc, chamber) or "")
        parsed = DataService._parse_bill_document(vote.get("document", ""))
        if rc["class"] != "D" or not parsed:
            continue
        key = f"{vote['congress']}-{parsed[0]}-{parsed[1]}"
        if key not in bills:
            continue
        when = _parse_vote_date(vote.get("vote_date", ""))
        rc["date"] = when.strftime("%Y-%m-%d") if when else ""
        rc["n"] = vote.get("vote_number") or 0
        current = latest.setdefault(key, {}).get(chamber)
        if current is None or (rc["date"], rc["n"]) > (current["date"], current["n"]):
            latest[key][chamber] = rc
    for key, per_chamber in latest.items():
        status = bill_status(bills[key].get("laws"), per_chamber, bills[key]["type"])
        assert status["text"] != "No final vote yet", key
    # "115 bills with no decisive vote" (spec §7.1) is approximate: the real
    # number is whatever this table yields, and it must stay a small minority.
    without_d = len(set(bills) - set(latest))
    assert 0 < without_d < len(bills) / 10
    joined = " ".join(outputs).lower()
    for word in FORBIDDEN:
        assert word not in joined


# --- §7.2 thresholds, seals and outcome phrases ---

def test_parse_threshold():
    assert parse_threshold("Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected (52-46, 3/5 majority required)") == "3/5"
    assert parse_threshold("Veto Sustained (60-37, 2/3 majority required)") == "2/3"
    assert parse_threshold("Passed", "Vote to pass (fast-track, needed two-thirds)") == "2/3"
    assert parse_threshold("Passed", "Final vote to pass") is None
    # The concur row has no threshold, but a suspension question implies two-thirds (16 real
    # "On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur…" roll calls); same rule as site.js twoThirdsNeeded.
    concur = "Vote to accept the other chamber's changes"
    assert parse_threshold("Failed", concur, "On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendment") == "2/3"
    assert parse_threshold("Passed", concur, "On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment") is None
    assert parse_threshold("Passed", "Procedural vote", "On Motion to Refer the Veto Message") is None

def test_result_phrase(question, result, counts, chamber, seal):
    assert _phrase(question, result, counts, chamber) == seal


def test_result_phrase_reads_the_index_threshold_and_any_chamber_spelling():
    rc = _rc("On Passage", "Failed", {"yeas": 250, "nays": 170})
    rc["threshold"] = "2/3"
    assert result_phrase(rc, "house") == "Rejected by the House 250–170 (two-thirds needed)"
    rc = _rc("On Passage", "Passed", {"yeas": 237, "nays": 169})
    del rc["plain"], rc["class"]  # classified from the question string
    assert result_phrase(rc, "House of Representatives") == "Passed the House 237–169"

# --- §7.2 bill status seal ---

def _d(plain, result, yeas, nays, iso_date, bill=None):
    return {"plain": plain, "class": "D", "result": result, "counts": {"yeas": yeas, "nays": nays},
            "date": iso_date, "bill": bill}


PASS = "Final vote to pass"
ADOPT = "Vote to adopt"


def test_bill_status_became_law_wins():
    laws = [{"number": "119-6", "type": "Public Law"}]
    assert bill_status(laws, {"House": _d(PASS, "Failed", 1, 2, "2026-01-01")}, "hr") == {
        "text": "Became law", "variant": "final"}


def test_bill_status_both_chambers():
    latest = {"House": _d(PASS, "Passed", 237, 169, "2026-09-03"),
              "Senate": _d(PASS, "Bill Passed (90-6)", 90, 6, "2026-09-10")}
    assert bill_status(None, latest, "hr") == {"text": "Passed both chambers", "variant": "final"}


def test_bill_status_one_chamber_is_moving_unless_simple_resolution():
    assert bill_status([], {"House": _d(PASS, "Passed", 237, 169, "2026-09-03"), "Senate": None}, "hr") == {
        "text": "Passed the House 237–169", "variant": "moving"}
    assert bill_status([], {"House": _d(ADOPT, "Passed", 220, 210, "2026-09-03")}, "hres") == {
        "text": "Adopted by the House 220–210", "variant": "final"}
    assert bill_status([], {"Senate": _d(ADOPT, "Joint Resolution Passed (51-47)", 51, 47, "2026-05-01")},
                       "sjres") == {"text": "Adopted by the Senate 51–47", "variant": "moving"}
    # Without bill_type, the simple resolution is recognised from the roll call's bill key.
    latest = {"House": _d(ADOPT, "Passed", 217, 204, "2021-01-04", "117-hres-8")}
    assert bill_status([], latest)["variant"] == "final"


def test_bill_status_chambers_differ_states_the_newer():
    latest = {"House": _d(PASS, "Passed", 237, 169, "2026-03-01"),
              "Senate": _d(PASS, "Bill Defeated (45-55)", 45, 55, "2026-04-01")}
    assert bill_status(None, latest, "hr") == {"text": "Rejected by the Senate 45–55", "variant": "moving"}


def test_bill_status_no_decisive_vote():
    assert bill_status(None, {}, "s") == {"text": "No final vote yet", "variant": "moving"}
    assert bill_status(None, {"House": None, "Senate": None}, "s")["text"] == "No final vote yet"


def test_bill_status_ignores_impeachment_verdicts():
    verdict = _d("Verdict on an article of impeachment (needed two-thirds)", "Not Guilty", 57, 43, "2021-02-13")
    assert bill_status(None, {"Senate": verdict}, "hres")["text"] == "No final vote yet"


# --- §7.1 positions ---

@pytest.mark.parametrize("vote, text, variant, short", [
    ("Yea", "Voted yes", "yes", "Yes"),
    ("Aye", "Voted yes", "yes", "Yes"),
    ("Nay", "Voted no", "no", "No"),
    ("No", "Voted no", "no", "No"),
    ("Not Voting", "Didn't vote", "nv", "Didn't vote"),
    ("Present", "Present", "present", "Present"),
    ("Present, Giving Live Pair", "Present", "present", "Present"),
    ("Guilty", "Guilty", "other", "Guilty"),
    ("Not Guilty", "Not Guilty", "other", "Not Guilty"),
    ("Jeffries", "Voted", "other", "Voted"),
    ("Johnson (LA)", "Voted", "other", "Voted"),
])
def test_position_chip(vote, text, variant, short):
    assert position_chip(vote) == {"text": text, "variant": variant, "short": short}


def test_position_chip_never_returns_candidate_name():
    assert "Jeffries" not in json.dumps(position_chip("Jeffries"))


# --- Dates ---

@pytest.mark.parametrize("value, short, expected", [
    ("2026-09-03", False, "September 3, 2026"),
    ("2026-09-03T00:00:00", False, "September 3, 2026"),
    ("2026-08-08T04:36:00", True, "Aug 8, 2026"),
    ("2026-09-03", True, "Sep 3, 2026"),
    ("", False, ""),
    (None, True, ""),
    ("not a date", False, "not a date"),
])
def test_format_date(value, short, expected):
    assert format_date(value, short=short) == expected


def test_format_date_default_is_long_and_accepts_a_style_string():
    assert format_date("2026-11-03") == "November 3, 2026"
    assert format_date("2026-11-03", "short") == "Nov 3, 2026"
    assert format_date("2026-11-03", "long") == "November 3, 2026"


def test_format_date_has_no_zero_padding_or_time():
    assert not re.search(r"\b0\d\b|:\d\d", format_date("2026-01-05T17:31:00"))
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `app/render.py`.**

```python
"""Pure formatters shared by the server-rendered pages and the API (spec §7, §9.1).

Every function here is pure: no I/O, no DataService access. site.js mirrors the
tables in this module (QUESTION_CLASSES here; the bill-type map arrives with the
naming formatters) and a parity test keeps the two in step, so the Python and JS
vocabularies can never drift apart.
"""
import re
from datetime import date

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# §7.1 question classes. Ordered: the first matching pattern wins. Each pattern
# is compiled with re.IGNORECASE and uses no Python-only syntax, so site.js
# mirrors a row as {pattern: row["pattern"].pattern, flags: "i", …}.
# "threshold" is the threshold the question itself implies (House suspension,
# veto, treaty, impeachment); a Senate result's "(3/5 majority required)" /
# "(2/3 majority required)" overrides it (see parse_threshold).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
QUESTION_CLASSES = [
    {"id": "pass", "class": "D", "plain": "Final vote to pass", "noun": None, "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On Passage\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "pass_fast", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to pass (fast-track, needed two-thirds)", "noun": None,
     "threshold": "2/3",
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On (the )?Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "adopt", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to adopt", "noun": None, "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(
         r"^On Agreeing to the Resolution\b|^On the (Joint |Concurrent )?Resolution\b(?! of Ratification)",
         re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "adopt_fast", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to adopt (fast-track, needed two-thirds)", "noun": None,
     "threshold": "2/3",
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On (the )?Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "concur", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to accept the other chamber's changes", "noun": None,
     "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(
         r"^On (the )?Motion to (Suspend the Rules and )?Concur\b|^On the Motion \(Motion to Concur\b"
         # A named mover ("Schumer Motion to Concur …") is the same vote, unless that senator's
         # motion adds an amendment ("… with an Amendment No. 1634"), which stays procedural.
         r"|^On the Motion \([A-Z][\w ()]*? Motion to Concur\b(?!.*\bwith an Amendment\b)"
         r"|^On the Motion \(Senate Concurs\b|^On Concurring\b",
         re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "veto", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to override the veto (needed two-thirds)", "noun": None,
     "threshold": "2/3",
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^Passage, Objections of the President|^On Overriding the Veto\b|^On the Veto\b",
                           re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "treaty", "class": "D", "plain": "Vote to ratify a treaty (needed two-thirds)", "noun": None,
     "threshold": "2/3",
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On the Resolution of Ratification\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "impeach", "class": "D", "plain": "Verdict on an article of impeachment (needed two-thirds)",
     "noun": None, "threshold": "2/3",
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^Guilty or Not Guilty\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "amendment", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote on an amendment", "noun": "an amendment", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On Agreeing to the Amendment\b|^On the Amendment\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "cloture", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to end debate (needed 60)", "noun": "a motion to end debate",
     "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed\b|^On the Cloture Motion\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "proceed", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to take it up", "noun": "a motion to take it up",
     "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On the Motion to Proceed\b|^Motion to Proceed\b|^On the Motion \(Motion to Proceed\b",
                           re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "recommit", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to send it back to committee",
     "noun": "a motion to send it back to committee", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(
         r"^On (the )?Motion to (Recommit|Commit|Refer)\b"
         r"|^On the Motion \((?!Motion to Waive).*\bMotions? to (Recommit|Commit|Refer)\b",
         re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "table", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to set it aside", "noun": "a motion to set it aside",
     "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On (the )?Motion to Table\b|^Table Motion to Reconsider\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "previous_question", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to end debate on the rule",
     "noun": "a motion to end debate on the rule", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On Ordering the Previous Question\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "discharge", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to bring it to the floor",
     "noun": "a motion to bring it to the floor", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On (the )?Motion to Discharge\b|^On the Motion \(Motion to Discharge\b",
                           re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "waive", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to waive a budget rule (needed 60)",
     "noun": "a motion to waive a budget rule", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On the Motion \(Motion to Waive\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "point_of_order", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote on a point of order", "noun": "a point of order",
     "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On the Point of Order\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "nomination", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to confirm", "noun": None, "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On the Nomination\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "speaker", "class": "P", "plain": "Election of the Speaker", "noun": None, "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^Election of the Speaker\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "adjourn", "class": "P", "plain": "Vote to adjourn", "noun": "a motion to adjourn", "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^On (the )?Motion to Adjourn\b", re.IGNORECASE)},
    {"id": "attendance", "class": "P", "plain": "Attendance call", "noun": None, "threshold": None,
     "pattern": re.compile(r"^Call of the House\b|^Call by States\b|^(On the )?Motion for Attendance\b",
                           re.IGNORECASE)},
]

# Any question no row matches.
PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK = {"id": "procedural", "class": "P", "plain": "Procedural vote",
                       "noun": "a procedural motion", "threshold": None, "pattern": None}

_ROW_BY_PLAIN = {row["plain"]: row for row in QUESTION_CLASSES + [PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK]}


def classify(question: str | None) -> dict:
    """The §7.1 table row for a roll-call question (first match wins)."""
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (question or "").strip())
    for row in QUESTION_CLASSES:
        if row["pattern"].search(text):
            return row
    return PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK


def question_class(question: str | None) -> str:
    """'D' (decisive: the vote on the measure itself) or 'P' (procedural)."""
    return classify(question)["class"]


def plain_question(question: str | None) -> str:
    """The plain-English name of a roll-call question, e.g. 'Final vote to pass'."""
    return classify(question)["plain"]


def _row(rc: dict) -> dict:
    """The table row for a votes_index roll call: by its stored plain question,
    else by classifying its question string."""
    return _ROW_BY_PLAIN.get(rc.get("plain") or "") or classify(rc.get("question"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dates (§7.3): long "September 3, 2026" in sentences, short "Sep 3, 2026" in meta.
# Month names are spelled out here so the output never depends on the locale.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_MONTHS_LONG = ("January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July",
                "August", "September", "October", "November", "December")
_MONTHS_SHORT = ("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")


def format_date(value: str | None, short: bool | str = False) -> str:
    """'2026-09-03' or '2026-09-03T00:00:00' -> 'September 3, 2026', or 'Sep 3, 2026'
    with short=True (a style string "short" / "long" is accepted too). Empty input
    -> ''. Input that is not an ISO date is returned stripped; never raises."""
    if isinstance(short, str):
        short = short == "short"
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return ""
    try:
        d = date.fromisoformat(text[:10])
    except ValueError:
        return text
    months = _MONTHS_SHORT if short else _MONTHS_LONG
    return f"{months[d.month - 1]} {d.day}, {d.year}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# §7.2 result -> seal text; §7.3 outcome sentence. `rc` is one votes_index.json
# roll_calls entry (question, plain, class, result, counts {yeas, nays, present,
# absent}, date, threshold); `chamber` is "House" or "Senate" (any case, and
# "House of Representatives", are accepted).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_PASSED_RE = re.compile(r"(Passed|Agreed to|Veto Overridden)$", re.IGNORECASE)
_FAILED_RE = re.compile(r"(Failed|Defeated|Rejected|Not Sustained|Veto Sustained)$", re.IGNORECASE)
_THRESHOLD_RE = re.compile(r"\((?:[^)]*?,\s*)?(3/5|2/3) majority required\)")
_VP_RE = re.compile(r"Vice President", re.IGNORECASE)
_NEEDED = {"2/3": "two-thirds needed", "3/5": "60 needed"}
_NEEDED_SENTENCE = {"2/3": "two-thirds were needed", "3/5": "60 votes were needed"}


def _chamber_name(chamber: str | None) -> str:
    return "Senate" if (chamber or "").strip().lower().startswith("senate") else "House"


def _other_chamber(chamber: str | None) -> str:
    return "House" if _chamber_name(chamber) == "Senate" else "Senate"


def _result_text(result: str | None) -> str:
    """The result string before its parenthesis: 'Bill Passed (90-6, …)' -> 'Bill Passed'."""
    return (result or "").split("(", 1)[0].strip()


# A question that implies two-thirds whatever its table row says (a suspension-concur row
# has none of its own). site.js twoThirdsNeeded (G2) tests the same alternation.
_TWO_THIRDS_QUESTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"Suspend the Rules|Objections of the President|Overriding the Veto|^On the Veto\b", re.IGNORECASE)


def parse_threshold(result: str | None, plain: str | None = None, question: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """'2/3' or '3/5' from a Senate result's '(… majority required)', else the
    threshold the plain question implies (suspension, veto, treaty, impeachment),
    else '2/3' when the raw question names a suspension or a veto, else None.
    sync.py's votes index stores exactly this as `threshold` (one formatter, §7.2)."""
    match = _THRESHOLD_RE.search(result or "")
    if match:
        return match.group(1)
    implied = _ROW_BY_PLAIN.get(plain or "", PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK)["threshold"]
    if implied:
        return implied
    return "2/3" if _TWO_THIRDS_QUESTION_RE.search(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (question or "").strip())) else None


def _outcome(result: str | None) -> str:
    """'passed', 'failed' or 'other' for a result string."""
    text = _result_text(result)
    if _FAILED_RE.search(text):
        return "failed"
    if _PASSED_RE.search(text):
        return "passed"
    return "other"


def _counts(rc: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
    counts = rc.get("counts") or {}
    return int(counts.get("yeas") or 0), int(counts.get("nays") or 0)


def result_phrase(rc: dict, chamber: str | None) -> str:
    """Seal text for one roll call (§7.2), e.g. 'Passed the House 237–169'."""
    row = _row(rc)
    cls = rc.get("class") or row["class"]
    result = rc.get("result")
    ch = _chamber_name(chamber)
    yeas, nays = _counts(rc)
    tally = f"{yeas}–{nays}"
    threshold = rc.get("threshold") or parse_threshold(result, row["plain"], rc.get("question"))
    needed = f" ({_NEEDED[threshold]})" if threshold in _NEEDED else ""
    outcome = _outcome(result)
    text = _result_text(result)

    if row["id"] == "speaker":
        return "Speaker elected"
    if row["id"] == "nomination":
        return text
    if yeas > 0 and yeas == nays and outcome in ("passed", "failed"):
        if outcome == "passed" and _VP_RE.search(result or ""):
            return f"Tied {tally} — agreed to on the Vice President's vote"
        return f"Tied {tally} — motion failed"

    if cls == "D":
        if row["id"] == "impeach":
            verdict = {"not guilty": "Not guilty", "guilty": "Guilty"}.get(text.lower(), text)
            return f"{verdict} {tally} ({_NEEDED['2/3']})"
        if row["id"] == "veto":
            if outcome == "passed":
                return f"Veto overridden in the {ch} {tally}"
            if outcome == "failed":
                return f"Veto override failed {tally} ({_NEEDED['2/3']})"
            return text
        if outcome == "passed":
            if row["id"] in ("adopt", "adopt_fast", "treaty"):
                return f"Adopted by the {ch} {tally}"
            return f"Passed the {ch} {tally}"
        if outcome == "failed":
            return f"Rejected by the {ch} {tally}{needed}"
        return text

    if row["id"] == "cloture":
        if outcome == "passed":
            return f"Debate ended {tally}"
        if outcome == "failed":
            return f"Debate not ended {tally} ({_NEEDED.get(threshold or '3/5', _NEEDED['3/5'])})"
        return text
    if row["id"] == "amendment":
        if outcome == "passed":
            return f"Amendment adopted {tally}"
        if outcome == "failed":
            return f"Amendment rejected {tally}{needed}"
        return text
    if outcome == "passed":
        return f"Motion agreed to {tally}"
    if outcome == "failed":
        return f"Motion rejected {tally}{needed}"
    return text


def outcome_sentence(rc: dict, chamber: str | None) -> str | None:
    """One-sentence outcome (§7.3) dated from rc['date']. None for Speaker
    elections and nominations (records and seals never show those sentences)."""
    row = _row(rc)
    if row["id"] in ("speaker", "nomination"):
        return None
    cls = rc.get("class") or row["class"]
    result = rc.get("result")
    ch = _chamber_name(chamber)
    yeas, nays = _counts(rc)
    when = format_date(rc.get("date"))
    threshold = rc.get("threshold") or parse_threshold(result, row["plain"], rc.get("question"))
    outcome = _outcome(result)
    text = _result_text(result)

    if yeas > 0 and yeas == nays and outcome in ("passed", "failed"):
        how = ("passed on the Vice President's vote"
               if outcome == "passed" and _VP_RE.search(result or "") else "failed")
        return f"The {ch} tied, {yeas} to {nays}, on {when}; the motion {how}."
    if row["id"] == "impeach":
        return f"On {when}, the {ch} voted {yeas} to {nays}; two-thirds were needed to convict."
    if outcome == "other":
        return f"On {when}, the {ch} voted {yeas} to {nays}: {text}."

    if cls == "D":
        if row["id"] == "veto":
            verb = "voted to override the veto" if outcome == "passed" else "did not override the veto"
            return f"The {ch} {verb}, {yeas} to {nays}, on {when}."
        if outcome == "passed":
            if row["id"] in ("adopt", "adopt_fast", "treaty"):
                verb = "adopted it"
            elif row["id"] == "concur":
                verb = f"accepted the {_other_chamber(chamber)}'s changes"
            else:
                verb = "passed it"
            return f"The {ch} {verb}, {yeas} to {nays}, on {when}."
        sentence = f"The {ch} rejected it, {yeas} to {nays}, on {when}"
        if threshold in _NEEDED_SENTENCE:
            sentence += f"; {_NEEDED_SENTENCE[threshold]}"
        return sentence + "."

    if row["id"] == "cloture":
        if outcome == "passed":
            return f"On {when}, the {ch} voted to end debate, {yeas} to {nays}."
        need = _NEEDED_SENTENCE.get(threshold or "3/5", _NEEDED_SENTENCE["3/5"])
        return f"On {when}, the {ch} voted {yeas} to {nays} to end debate; {need}, so debate did not end."
    if row["id"] == "amendment":
        verb = "adopted an amendment" if outcome == "passed" else "rejected an amendment"
    else:
        noun = row["noun"] or PROCEDURAL_FALLBACK["noun"]
        verb = f"agreed to {noun}" if outcome == "passed" else f"rejected {noun}"
    return f"On {when}, the {ch} {verb}, {yeas} to {nays}."


def bill_status(laws: list | None, latest_by_chamber: dict | None, bill_type: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Bill status seal (§7.2): {'text': ..., 'variant': 'final' | 'moving'}.

    latest_by_chamber maps 'House' / 'Senate' (any case) to that chamber's newest
    class-D votes_index roll call, or None. Impeachment verdicts are never a bill
    seal. A simple resolution (H.Res./S.Res.) is recognised from bill_type or, when
    that is omitted, from the roll call's `bill` key ("119-hres-8")."""
    if laws:
        return {"text": "Became law", "variant": "final"}
    votes = {}
    for chamber, rc in (latest_by_chamber or {}).items():
        if not rc or _row(rc)["id"] == "impeach":
            continue
        votes[_chamber_name(chamber)] = rc
    if not votes:
        return {"text": "No final vote yet", "variant": "moving"}
    passed = {ch: _outcome(rc.get("result")) == "passed" for ch, rc in votes.items()}
    if len(votes) == 2 and all(passed.values()):
        return {"text": "Passed both chambers", "variant": "final"}
    # One chamber voted, or the chambers differ / both rejected: state the newer.
    ch, rc = max(votes.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1].get("date") or "", item[0]))
    kind = (bill_type or "").lower() or ((rc.get("bill") or "").split("-") + ["", ""])[1]
    variant = "final" if passed[ch] and kind in ("hres", "sres") else "moving"
    return {"text": result_phrase(rc, ch), "variant": variant}


# §7.1 positions -> chip text, variant (the .chip--{variant} class) and the
# short form printed inside roll-call tables. Guilty / Not Guilty are verbatim.
_POSITIONS = {
    "yea": ("Voted yes", "yes", "Yes"),
    "aye": ("Voted yes", "yes", "Yes"),
    "nay": ("Voted no", "no", "No"),
    "no": ("Voted no", "no", "No"),
    "not voting": ("Didn't vote", "nv", "Didn't vote"),
    "present": ("Present", "present", "Present"),
    "present, giving live pair": ("Present", "present", "Present"),
    "guilty": ("Guilty", "other", "Guilty"),
    "not guilty": ("Not Guilty", "other", "Not Guilty"),
}


def position_chip(vote: str | None) -> dict:
    """{'text', 'variant', 'short'} for a member's recorded position. Any other
    string (a Speaker-election candidate name) is 'Voted' — the name itself is
    shown only with the party reveal (§4.3)."""
    text, variant, short = _POSITIONS.get((vote or "").strip().lower(), ("Voted", "other", "Voted"))
    return {"text": text, "variant": variant, "short": short}
```

```python
"""SSR escaping registry (spec §9.1, §10 #22).

Every renderer that puts data into HTML is registered in RENDERERS with a
callable that embeds the hostile payload it is given somewhere in its output
(as a name, title, headline, …). Each later render task appends its block
renderers here, so one test covers every renderer against every payload."""
import re

import pytest

from app.render import display_name, format_bill_code, h, sponsor_name

HOSTILE = [
    "<script>alert(1)</script>",
    '"><img src=x>',
    "&amp;",
    "javascript:alert(1)",
]

RENDERERS = {
    "h": lambda p: h(p),
    "h(display_name)": lambda p: h(display_name(f"{p}, {p}")),
    "h(format_bill_code)": lambda p: h(format_bill_code("hr", p)),
    "h(sponsor_name)": lambda p: h(sponsor_name(
        {"fullName": f"Rep. {p}", "firstName": p, "lastName": p, "state": "NY"})),
}


def assert_escaped(out: str, payload: str) -> None:
    lowered = out.lower()
    assert "<script" not in lowered
    assert "<img" not in lowered
    assert not re.search(r"""(href|src)\s*=\s*["']?\s*javascript:""", lowered)
    if payload == "&amp;":
        # The literal entity text was escaped, not passed through as markup.
        assert "&amp;amp;" in out
    if payload.startswith('"'):
        # The attribute-breaking payload never appears raw. (Not '"><' in general: every
        # block renderer's own markup, e.g. class="page-error"><h1>, contains that.)
        assert payload not in out


@pytest.mark.parametrize("payload", HOSTILE)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", sorted(RENDERERS))
def test_renderer_escapes_hostile_input(name, payload):
    assert_escaped(RENDERERS[name](payload), payload)


def test_hostile_fixture_title_is_escaped():
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    bills = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "synced" / "bills.json").read_text())["bills"]
    title = next(b["title"] for b in bills if b["number"] == "99999")
    out = h(title)
    assert "<b>" not in out and "&lt;b&gt;" in out
    assert "&amp;" in out and "&quot;" in out and "&#x27;" in out
```

```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# §9.1 escaping, §7.5 codes / names / tenure, §7.4 seat seals, §4.4 sponsor,
# §10 #10 tag stripping.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def h(value) -> str:
    """The one escape helper: every interpolated data value in rendered HTML goes
    through this. None renders as an empty string."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    return html.escape(str(value), quote=True)


# Title-case bill abbreviations, e.g. "hr" -> "H.R." (moved from app/main.py;
# site.js carries the same map and test_formatter_parity keeps them equal).
_BILL_TYPE_LABELS = {
    "hr": "H.R.",
    "s": "S.",
    "hjres": "H.J.Res.",
    "sjres": "S.J.Res.",
    "hconres": "H.Con.Res.",
    "sconres": "S.Con.Res.",
    "hres": "H.Res.",
    "sres": "S.Res.",
}


def format_bill_code(bill_type: str | None, number) -> str:
    """('hr', 4795) -> 'H.R. 4795'; unknown types fall back to the upper-cased type."""
    raw = (bill_type or "").strip()
    label = _BILL_TYPE_LABELS.get(raw.lower(), raw.upper())
    return f"{label} {str(number).strip()}".strip()


def ordinal(n) -> str:
    """119 -> '119th', 1 -> '1st', 112 -> '112th' (11–13 always take 'th')."""
    n = int(n)
    if 11 <= n % 100 <= 13:
        suffix = "th"
    else:
        suffix = {1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd"}.get(n % 10, "th")
    return f"{n}{suffix}"


def display_name(name: str | None) -> str:
    """'Schumer, Charles E.' -> 'Charles E. Schumer'. members.json has no
    directOrderName, so this is the only path from the stored name to a display name."""
    text = (name or "").strip()
    if "," not in text:
        return text
    last, first = text.split(",", 1)
    return f"{first.strip()} {last.strip()}".strip()


def _term_chamber(term: dict) -> str:
    return "Senate" if (term.get("chamber") or "").lower().startswith("senate") else "House"


def tenure_line(terms) -> str:
    """'In Congress since 2025' for one chamber; 'In Congress since 1981 — House
    1981–1999, Senate since 1999' for two. Accepts members.json `terms` ({'item': [...]})
    or the bare list."""
    items = terms.get("item", []) if isinstance(terms, dict) else list(terms or [])
    spans: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for term in items:
        start = term.get("startYear")
        if not start:
            continue
        span = spans.setdefault(_term_chamber(term), {"start": start, "end": None, "current": False})
        span["start"] = min(span["start"], start)
        if term.get("endYear"):
            span["end"] = max(span["end"] or 0, term["endYear"])
        else:
            span["current"] = True
    if not spans:
        return ""
    first = min(span["start"] for span in spans.values())
    if len(spans) == 1:
        return f"In Congress since {first}"
    parts = []
    for chamber, span in sorted(spans.items(), key=lambda item: item[1]["start"]):
        if span["current"] or not span["end"]:
            parts.append(f"{chamber} since {span['start']}")
        else:
            parts.append(f"{chamber} {span['start']}–{span['end']}")
    return f"In Congress since {first} — " + ", ".join(parts)


# §7.4: ballot copy describes the SEAT, never the person.
_SEAT_SEALS = {
    ("regular", "row"): "Seat up Nov 3",
    ("regular", "header"): "This seat is on the ballot Nov 3, 2026",
    ("special", "row"): "Special election Nov 3",
    ("special", "header"): "Special election for this seat Nov 3, 2026",
}


def seat_seal(kind: str | None, context: str = "row", header: bool = False) -> str:
    """Seat seal text for data_service.seat_up_2026(member) ('regular' | 'special' | None):
    the row form by default, the member-header form with context="header" or
    header=True. '' when the seat is not up (no negative ballot copy exists)."""
    where = "header" if header or context == "header" else "row"
    return _SEAT_SEALS.get((kind or "", where), "")


_SPONSOR_PREFIXES = r"(Rep\.|Sen\.|Del\.|Rescom\.|Resident Commissioner)"
# The [R-AL-6] suffix is optional: T1.8's page sponsor already carries fullName
# without it ("Rep. Smith, Jason"), and G7 renders that dict through sponsor_name.
_SPONSOR_FULLNAME_RE = re.compile(rf"^{_SPONSOR_PREFIXES}\s+(.+?)\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$")
_SPONSOR_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(rf"^{_SPONSOR_PREFIXES}\s")


def _name_part(part: str | None) -> str:
    """Fallback only: 176 real sponsors carry ALL-CAPS firstName/lastName ('STENY')."""
    part = (part or "").strip()
    return part.title() if part.isupper() else part


def sponsor_name(sponsor: dict | None) -> str:
    """'Rep. Gary J. Palmer (AL)' from 'Rep. Palmer, Gary J. [R-AL-6]' + state: the
    prefix is kept, the 'Last, First M.' part goes through display_name, and the
    [R-AL-6] suffix (party letter) is dropped. fullName is the primary source
    because firstName/lastName are ALL CAPS on 176 real bills and lastName halves
    compound surnames ('Rodgers' for McMorris Rodgers). Falls back to
    firstName + lastName only when fullName does not parse."""
    sponsor = sponsor or {}
    full = (sponsor.get("fullName") or "").strip()
    match = _SPONSOR_FULLNAME_RE.match(full)
    if match and "," in match.group(2):
        prefix, person = match.group(1), display_name(match.group(2))
    else:
        prefix_match = _SPONSOR_PREFIX_RE.match(full)
        prefix = prefix_match.group(1) if prefix_match else ""
        person = " ".join(p for p in (_name_part(sponsor.get("firstName")),
                                      _name_part(sponsor.get("lastName"))) if p)
    if not person:
        return ""
    state = (sponsor.get("state") or "").strip()
    text = " ".join(p for p in (prefix, person) if p)
    return f"{text} ({state})" if state else text


class _TextOnly(HTMLParser):
    """Collects text nodes only; drops every tag, attribute and the contents of
    <script>/<style>. Entities are decoded (convert_charrefs), so callers must
    still pass the result through h() before it reaches HTML."""

    _SKIP = {"script", "style"}

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.parts: list[str] = []
        self._skip_depth = 0

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag in self._SKIP:
            self._skip_depth += 1
        elif tag in ("p", "br", "li", "div"):
            self.parts.append(" ")

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in self._SKIP and self._skip_depth:
            self._skip_depth -= 1

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if not self._skip_depth:
            self.parts.append(data)


def strip_tags(markup: str | None) -> str:
    """Plain text from an HTML fragment, whitespace collapsed (§10 #10)."""
    parser = _TextOnly()
    parser.feed(markup or "")
    parser.close()
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", "".join(parser.parts)).strip()
```

  - `sync.votes_index_payload(sync_dir: Path) -> dict`: a pure function returning `{"roll_calls", "bills", "latest"}` with no `generated_at`.

    - `bills`: `{"119-hr-4795": {"roll_calls": [keys newest first], "activity_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null}}`. It covers every bill in `bills.json` and every bill a roll call names.
    - `latest`: the newest roll-call key on a bill in `bills.json`. Within a day, a class-D vote comes before a class-P vote, and then the higher vote number wins. It is null when there is none.

**Resolves:** spec §10 #3, §7.1 (class per roll call; the count of bills with no decisive vote is computed and printed, never hard-coded), §7.3 (Senate display dates become ISO at sync), §9.6 (startup loads one index instead of 5,369 files), §2.5 item 8; findings F05 (the runtime stops scanning vote files), F01 (activity date so the Record can show the newest activity), F32 (no raw timestamps or double spaces from Senate dates).

```python
def roll_call_key(chamber, congress, session, vote_number) -> str:
    """The votes_index.json key of one roll call, e.g. 'house/119_2_00295' (spec §10 #3).

    `chamber` is 'House'/'Senate' in member_votes rows and 'house'/'senate' for the vote
    directories; both give the same key. A missing part raises TypeError/ValueError."""
    return f"{str(chamber).strip().lower()}/{int(congress)}_{int(session)}_{int(vote_number):05d}"
```
