  ```js
  /* bill-slot:start */
  /* ============================================
     Bill page: "How did your representatives vote?" slot
     (plan T7.3; spec §4.4 m2, §5.2, §5.4 write rule 3, §8 items 10–11).
     Called only by bill.js; every entry point returns early when the slot is
     not on the page. Rows, chips, the remembered line, cv-home and focus all go
     through the shared helpers above (personRow, chip, rememberedLine, readHome,
     rememberDistrict, rewriteMastheadLink, focusHeading); DOM via el() only.
     ============================================ */

  const SLOT_ZIP_RE = /^\s*(\d{5})(?:[-\s]?\d{4})?\s*$/;
  const SLOT_BIOGUIDE_RE = /^[A-Z]\d{6}$/;
  const SLOT_HOUSE_GOV = 'https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative';
  const SLOT_COUNT_WORDS = ['zero', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four'];
  let slotFormTemplate = null;

  // A chamber has a roll call on this bill when any block, rendered or collapsed, names it (T7.2).
  function slotChamberHasRollCall(chamber) {
      return Boolean(document.querySelector(`[data-chamber="${chamber}"]`));
  }

  // This bill's chip for one current member, read from the server-rendered rows (no fetch): the
  // row's position, or the grey "Not in the {chamber} for this vote" chip when the member is absent.
  function slotSignal(member, chamber, label) {
      const block = document.querySelector(`.rc-block[data-rendered="1"][data-chamber="${chamber}"]`);
      if (!block) return el('span', { className: 'person-signal meta' }, t('rollCallsBelow', { chamber: label }));
      const row = block.querySelector(`tr[data-bioguide="${member.bioguideId}"]`);
      return el('span', { className: 'person-signal' }, chip(row ? row.dataset.position : null, { chamber: label }));
  }

  function slotStatus(text, isError) {
      const status = document.getElementById('reps-zip-status');
      if (!status) return;
      status.textContent = text;
      status.classList.toggle('is-error', Boolean(isError));
  }

  function slotLink(href, text) {
      return el('a', { href, rel: href.startsWith('https://') ? 'noopener' : null }, text);
  }

  // Puts the untouched server form back (Forget, or no cv-home); returns the slot body so
  // rememberedLine can focus its first control.
  function slotRestoreForm() {
      const body = document.getElementById('your-reps-body');
      if (!body || !slotFormTemplate) return body;
      const form = slotFormTemplate.cloneNode(true);
      clear(body);
      body.appendChild(form);
      slotBindForm(form);
      slotStatus('', false);
      return body;
  }

  // Fills the slot from cv-home, or, when storage refused the write, from the reader's pick for
  // this view only (then without a "Remembered" line). Resolves true when the rows were drawn.
  async function fillRepsSlot(picked) {
      const body = document.getElementById('your-reps-body');
      if (!body) return false;
      const stored = readHome();
      const home = stored || picked || null;
      if (!home) {
          if (!body.querySelector('form')) slotRestoreForm();
          return false;
      }
      let overview;
      try {
          const res = await fetch(`/api/members/${encodeURIComponent(home.state)}/overview`);
          if (!res.ok) throw new Error('overview');
          overview = await res.json();
      } catch (e) {
          return false; /* the server-rendered ZIP form stays usable */
      }
      const house = (overview.house || []).find(
          (m) => m.district === home.district && SLOT_BIOGUIDE_RE.test(m.bioguideId || ''));
      const senators = (overview.senators || []).filter((m) => SLOT_BIOGUIDE_RE.test(m.bioguideId || ''));
      const list = el('div', { className: 'your-reps-list' });
      [['house', 'House'], ['senate', 'Senate']].forEach(([chamber, label]) => {
          if (!slotChamberHasRollCall(chamber)) {
              list.appendChild(el('p', { className: 'meta' }, t('noChamberVote', { chamber: label })));
          } else if (chamber === 'house') {
              list.appendChild(house
                  ? personRow(house, home.state, slotSignal(house, chamber, label))
                  : el('p', { className: 'meta' }, t('vacantDistrict', { district: home.district })));
          } else {
              senators.forEach((senator) => list.appendChild(
                  personRow(senator, home.state, slotSignal(senator, chamber, label))));
          }
      });
      if (stored) list.appendChild(rememberedLine(stored, () => slotRestoreForm()));
      clear(body);
      body.appendChild(list);
      return true;
  }

  // In-place result (split, partial, none): a one-line summary into the role=status node first,
  // then the note under the form, then focus to the slot heading (§8 items 10–11).
  function slotShowResult(node, statusText) {
      const body = document.getElementById('your-reps-body');
      if (!body) return;
      const previous = body.querySelector('.slot-result');
      if (previous) previous.remove();
      slotStatus(statusText, false);
      body.appendChild(node);
      focusHeading(document.getElementById('your-reps-h'));
  }

  // The reader's own act (a single-match submit or a District button): the only cv-home write here.
  async function slotPick(state, district) {
      if (!COVERED_STATES[state] || !Number.isInteger(district)) return;
      rememberDistrict(state, district);
      rewriteMastheadLink();
      document.querySelectorAll(`details.state-group[data-state="${state}"]`).forEach((d) => { d.open = true; });
      const filled = await fillRepsSlot({ state, district, savedAt: '' });
      if (!filled) slotStatus(t('pageError'), true);
      focusHeading(document.getElementById('your-reps-h'));
  }

  // Same wording as T4.1's server note: "ZIP 11201 spans two House districts — about 72 % of the
  // ZIP's land area (not its residents) is in District 10 and 28 % in District 7."
  function slotShareSentence(zip, matches, multiState) {
      const word = SLOT_COUNT_WORDS[matches.length] || String(matches.length);
      const pct = (m) => Math.round(Number(m.share || 0) * 100);
      const where = (m) => (multiState ? `${COVERED_STATES[m.state]} District ${m.district}` : `District ${m.district}`);
      const first = `about ${pct(matches[0])} % of the ZIP's land area (not its residents) is in ${where(matches[0])}`;
      const others = matches.slice(1).map((m) => `${pct(m)} % in ${where(m)}`);
      const shares = others.length === 1 ? `${first} and ${others[0]}`
          : `${first}, ${others.slice(0, -1).join(', ')} and ${others[others.length - 1]}`;
      return `ZIP ${zip} spans ${word} House districts — ${shares}. Your street address decides which is yours; choose it below.`;
  }

  function slotShowChoices(zip, data) {
      const matches = (data.matches || []).filter((m) => COVERED_STATES[m.state] && Number.isInteger(m.district));
      const multiState = new Set(matches.map((m) => m.state)).size > 1;
      const box = el('div', { className: 'note slot-result' });
      if (matches.length >= 2) box.appendChild(el('p', null, slotShareSentence(zip, matches, multiState)));
      const choices = el('div', { className: 'actions' });
      matches.forEach((m) => {
          const button = el('button', { type: 'button', className: 'btn btn--secondary' },
              multiState ? `${COVERED_STATES[m.state]}, District ${m.district}` : `District ${m.district}`);
          button.addEventListener('click', () => slotPick(m.state, m.district));
          choices.appendChild(button);
      });
      box.appendChild(choices);
      if (data.kind === 'partial') {
          const outside = Math.round((1 - Number(data.covered_share || 0)) * 100);
          box.appendChild(el('p', null, `About ${outside} % of ZIP ${zip}'s land area is outside California, Florida, New York and Texas; if you live in that part, we don't cover your state yet.`));
      }
      box.appendChild(el('p', null, slotLink(SLOT_HOUSE_GOV, 'Not sure? Look up your district by street address on house.gov →')));
      const count = SLOT_COUNT_WORDS[matches.length] || String(matches.length);
      slotShowResult(box, data.kind === 'split' ? t('zipSplitStatus', { zip, count }) : t('zipPartialStatus', { zip }));
  }

  function slotShowNotFound(zip) {
      const states = el('ul', { className: 'state-links' }, ...Object.keys(COVERED_STATES).map((code) =>
          el('li', null, el('a', { className: 'state-link', href: `/state?code=${code}` }, COVERED_STATES[code]))));
      const box = el('div', { className: 'note slot-result' },
          el('p', null,
              `We couldn't match ZIP ${zip} to a congressional district in California, Florida, New York or Texas — the four states ClearVoting covers. If you live in one of them, your ZIP may be a PO-box or business ZIP: choose your state below, or `,
              slotLink(SLOT_HOUSE_GOV, 'look up your district by street address on house.gov →'),
              '. ',
              slotLink(`/state?zip=${zip}`, "Somewhere else? Tell us your state and we'll email you when we add it.")),
          states);
      slotShowResult(box, t('zipNoneStatus', { zip }));
  }

  function slotBindForm(form) {
      form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          const input = form.querySelector('input[name="zip"]');
          const match = SLOT_ZIP_RE.exec(input ? input.value : '');
          slotStatus('', false);
          if (!match) {
              slotStatus(t('zipInvalid'), true);
              return;
          }
          const zip = match[1];
          let data;
          try {
              const res = await fetch(`/api/districts/${zip}`);
              if (res.status === 400) {
                  slotStatus(t('zipInvalid'), true);
                  return;
              }
              if (!res.ok) throw new Error('districts');
              data = await res.json();
          } catch (e) {
              slotStatus(t('pageError'), true);
              return;
          }
          if (data.kind === 'single' && Array.isArray(data.matches) && data.matches.length === 1) {
              await slotPick(data.matches[0].state, data.matches[0].district);
          } else if (data.kind === 'split' || data.kind === 'partial') {
              slotShowChoices(zip, data);
          } else {
              slotShowNotFound(zip);
          }
      });
  }

  function initZipInPlace() {
      if (!document.getElementById('your-reps')) return;
      const form = document.getElementById('reps-zip-form');
      if (form) {
          if (!slotFormTemplate) slotFormTemplate = form.cloneNode(true);
          slotBindForm(form);
      }
      window.addEventListener('pageshow', (event) => { if (event.persisted) fillRepsSlot(); });
  }
  /* bill-slot:end */

  ```

  (c) In the node export list at the end of the file, add one line directly above its closing `};`:
  ```js

  ```
  Rules this code follows (spec §5.4): `cv-home` is written only through T2.3's `rememberDistrict`, called only in `slotPick`, which runs only on the reader's own act (a single-match submit or a District button); a partial or split lookup writes nothing until a button is pressed; every write is followed by `rewriteMastheadLink()`, so "My representatives" points at the new district without a reload; Forget is T2.3's `rememberedLine` button, which removes the key, re-points the masthead link and focuses the first control of the restored server form; the in-place result writes its one-line summary into `#reps-zip-status` and moves focus to `#your-reps-h`.

  @app.get("/bill")
  def serve_bill(request: Request):
      """Server-rendered bill page (spec §4.4, §9.1). Unknown or malformed bill → 404."""
      from app.dependencies import get_data_service
      params = request.query_params
      bill_type = (params.get("type") or "").strip().lower()
      congress_raw = (params.get("congress") or "").strip()
      number_raw = (params.get("number") or "").strip()
      if not (congress_raw.isdigit() and number_raw.isdigit()) or bill_type not in VALID_BILL_TYPES:
          raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
      congress, number = int(congress_raw), int(number_raw)
      if not 1 <= congress <= 200:
          raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
      data_service = get_data_service()
      page = data_service.get_bill_page(congress, bill_type, number)
      if page is None:
          raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
      meta = _bill_meta(page)
      # T3.1: a render failure (a malformed roll-call file, a formatter exception) returns the §4
      # error state — masthead, the bill code as H1, "We couldn't load this page right now…" — with
      # 503 (no-store), not a bare 500 (F61).
      content, status = _page_content(
          lambda: render_bill_page(page, data_service.get_sync_metadata().get("ai_summaries_updated")),
          {**meta, "h1": format_bill_code(page["bill_type"], page["number"])},
      )
      return _serve_html("bill.html", meta, content, status_code=status)

- [ ] **Step 7 — Rewrite `static/js/vote.js`** (whole file). It keeps no positions table and no row builder of its own: rows are T2.2's `rcTableRow` (the DOM twin of the server's state-group rows — same key, link, seat and `chip(position, {short: true})`), and the filter reads the kind through `positionChip`:
  ```js
  /* ============================================
     ClearVoting — roll-call tables (bill page)
     Rows come from site.js rcTableRow (one vocabulary with the server, §10 #21);
     classes only: every colour lives in site.css (spec §6.1, §6.4).
     ============================================ */

  const RC_PARTY_NAMES = { D: 'Democratic', R: 'Republican', I: 'Independent', ID: 'Independent' };

  // Same key the server writes on each row (render._rc_row) and rcTableRow sets:
  // House by bioguide id, Senate by state + last name.
  function rcMemberKey(member, chamber) {
      return chamber === 'house'
          ? (member.bioguide_id || '')
          : `${member.state || ''}-${member.last_name || ''}`;
  }

  // render._rc_sorted_rows: 119th House by district (unknown last), else last name, first name.
  function rcSortMembers(members, chamber, current) {
      const byName = (a, b) => (a.last_name || '').localeCompare(b.last_name || '')
          || (a.first_name || '').localeCompare(b.first_name || '');
      const rows = members.slice();
      if (current && chamber === 'house') {
          const rank = (m) => (Number.isInteger(m.district) ? m.district : Infinity);
          return rows.sort((a, b) => (rank(a) - rank(b)) || byName(a, b));
      }
      return rows.sort(byName);
  }

  // current: a 119th-Congress roll call inside one state's group (district print and order).
  function buildRcTable(captionText, members, chamber, current) {
      const head = el('thead', null, el('tr', null,
          el('th', { scope: 'col' }, 'Member'), el('th', { scope: 'col' }, 'Vote')));
      const body = el('tbody', null, ...rcSortMembers(members, chamber, current)
          .map((member) => rcTableRow(member, { chamber, current })));
      return el('table', { className: 'rc' }, el('caption', null, captionText), head, body);
  }

  function filterRcRows(container, query, show) {
      const needle = (query || '').trim().toLowerCase();
      container.querySelectorAll('tbody tr').forEach((row) => {
          const found = positionChip(row.dataset.position);
          const kindMatches = show === 'all' || (found ? found[0] : 'nv') === show;
          const cell = row.querySelector('th');
          const name = cell && cell.firstChild ? cell.firstChild.textContent : '';
          row.hidden = !(kindMatches && (!needle || name.toLowerCase().includes(needle)));
      });
  }

  function fillPartySpans(container, members, chamber) {
      const partyByKey = new Map(members.map((m) => [rcMemberKey(m, chamber), m.party]));
      container.querySelectorAll('tbody tr[data-key]').forEach((row) => {
          const span = row.querySelector('.party');
          if (!span) return;
          const code = partyByKey.get(row.dataset.key);
          span.textContent = code ? ` · ${RC_PARTY_NAMES[code] || code}` : '';
      });
  }

  function clearPartySpans(container) {
      container.querySelectorAll('.party').forEach((span) => { span.textContent = ''; });
  }
  ```

- [ ] **Step 8 — Rewrite `static/js/bill.js`** (whole file). The first block is the existing `SAFE_TAGS`/`sanitizeHtml` block copied verbatim from the old lines 7–19:
  ```js
  /* ============================================
     ClearVoting — Bill page enhancer (spec §4.4)
     The server renders the page. This file adds only what needs a click or
     belongs to this reader: the official summary fill, the lazy roll-call
     lists, the party reveal and the "your representatives" slot.
     ============================================ */

  const SAFE_TAGS = new Set(['P', 'EM', 'STRONG', 'B', 'I', 'BR', 'UL', 'OL', 'LI', 'A']);
  function sanitizeHtml(html) {
      const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, 'text/html');
      doc.body.querySelectorAll('*').forEach(node => {
          if (!SAFE_TAGS.has(node.tagName)) {
              node.replaceWith(...node.childNodes);
          }
          for (const attr of [...node.attributes]) {
              if (attr.name !== 'href') node.removeAttribute(attr.name);
          }
      });
      return doc.body.innerHTML;
  }

  const BILL_RC_CACHE = new Map();
  let billPartyShown = false;

  function billFetchRollCall(url, withParty) {
      const full = withParty ? `${url}?show_party=true` : url;
      if (!BILL_RC_CACHE.has(full)) {
          const request = fetch(full)
              .then(res => {
                  if (!res.ok) throw new Error('roll call');
                  return res.json();
              })
              .catch(err => {
                  BILL_RC_CACHE.delete(full);
                  throw err;
              });
          BILL_RC_CACHE.set(full, request);
      }
      return BILL_RC_CACHE.get(full);
  }

  function billOpenHomeState(scope) {
      const home = readHome();
      if (!home) return;
      scope.querySelectorAll(`details.state-group[data-state="${home.state}"]`).forEach(group => { group.open = true; });
  }

  // The one sanctioned HTML sink. The four lines inside the if are byte-identical to baseline
  // bill.js lines 165–168 (June plan constraint 4); only the source changed: T1.8's
  // official_summary (Public Law first, else newest) instead of summaries[0] (the oldest).
  function billFillOfficialSummary(summaryDiv, latestSummary) {
      if (latestSummary) {
          summaryDiv.textContent = '';
          // Content is sanitized — only safe tags (P, EM, STRONG, B, I, BR, UL, OL, LI, A) remain
          const sanitized = sanitizeHtml(latestSummary);
          summaryDiv.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', sanitized);
      }
  }

  function billInitOfficialSummary(billId) {
      const slot = document.querySelector('details[data-summary-slot]');
      const summaryDiv = document.getElementById('official-summary-body');
      if (!slot || !summaryDiv) return;
      const [congress, type, number] = billId.split('-');
      let loaded = false;
      slot.addEventListener('toggle', async () => {
          if (!slot.open || loaded) return;
          loaded = true;
          summaryDiv.textContent = 'Loading summary…';
          try {
              const res = await fetch(`/api/bills/${encodeURIComponent(congress)}/${encodeURIComponent(type)}/${encodeURIComponent(number)}`);
              if (!res.ok) throw new Error('bill');
              const data = await res.json();
              billFillOfficialSummary(summaryDiv, data.official_summary || '');
          } catch (e) {
              loaded = false;
              summaryDiv.textContent = t('pageError');
          }
      });
  }

  function billInitAllVotes() {
      document.querySelectorAll('details.rc-all').forEach(details => {
          const list = details.querySelector('.rc-all-list');
          const query = details.querySelector('.rc-all-q');
          const show = details.querySelector('.rc-all-show');
          const block = details.closest('[data-chamber]');
          if (!list || !query || !show || !block) return;
          const apply = () => filterRcRows(list, query.value, show.value);
          let loaded = false;
          details.addEventListener('toggle', async () => {
              if (!details.open || loaded) return;
              loaded = true;
              try {
                  const data = await billFetchRollCall(details.dataset.url, billPartyShown);
                  const members = data.members || [];
                  clear(list);
                  // Every state in one table: sorted by name and each row shows its state, since
                  // "District 4" alone is ambiguous across states (current = false).
                  list.appendChild(buildRcTable(`Every state — ${details.dataset.caption}`, members, block.dataset.chamber, false));
                  if (billPartyShown) fillPartySpans(list, members, block.dataset.chamber);
                  apply();
              } catch (e) {
                  loaded = false;
                  list.textContent = t('pageError');
              }
          });
          query.addEventListener('input', apply);
          show.addEventListener('change', apply);
      });
  }

  function billInitExtraRollCalls() {
      document.querySelectorAll('details.rc-more').forEach(details => {
          const box = details.querySelector('.rc-groups');
          if (!box) return;
          let loaded = false;
          details.addEventListener('toggle', async () => {
              if (!details.open || loaded) return;
              loaded = true;
              const chamber = details.dataset.chamber;
              const current = details.dataset.current === '1';
              try {
                  const data = await billFetchRollCall(details.dataset.url, billPartyShown);
                  const members = data.members || [];
                  clear(box);
                  Object.keys(COVERED_STATES).forEach(code => {
                      const rows = members.filter(m => m.state === code);
                      if (!rows.length) return;
                      // The group summary is the block's own index tally line, so it reads exactly
                      // like the server's groups: "New York: 13 yes · 11 no · 2 didn't vote".
                      const tally = details.querySelector(`.state-tallies li[data-state="${code}"]`);
                      box.appendChild(el('details', { className: 'state-group', 'data-state': code },
                          el('summary', null, tally ? tally.textContent : COVERED_STATES[code]),
                          buildRcTable(`${COVERED_STATES[code]} — ${details.dataset.caption}`, rows, chamber, current)));
                  });
                  if (billPartyShown) fillPartySpans(box, members, chamber);
                  billOpenHomeState(box);
              } catch (e) {
                  loaded = false;
                  box.textContent = t('pageError');
              }
          });
      });
  }

  // Fill callback for site.js initPartyToggle: one page-level toggle covers every list (spec §4.4 m3).
  async function billSetParty(shown) {
      billPartyShown = shown;
      const containers = document.querySelectorAll('section.rc-block[data-url], details.rc-more[data-url]');
      for (const box of containers) {
          if (!shown) {
              clearPartySpans(box);
              continue;
          }
          if (!box.querySelector('tbody tr')) continue;
          try {
              const data = await billFetchRollCall(box.dataset.url, true);
              fillPartySpans(box, data.members || [], box.dataset.chamber);
          } catch (e) {
              /* names and positions stay; the party spans stay empty for this list */
          }
      }
  }

  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
      const root = document.querySelector('.bill-grid[data-bill]');
      if (!root) return;
      billInitOfficialSummary(root.dataset.bill);
      billInitAllVotes();
      billInitExtraRollCalls();
      billOpenHomeState(document);
      initPartyToggle(billSetParty);
      initShare();
      initZipInPlace();
      fillRepsSlot();
  });
  ```

The member and bill title formats, the 70-character official-title fallback, case-normalized member/bill canonicals and the member/bill 404s were resolved by T6.3 and T7.4; this task's tests re-check them end to end.

**Member `lastmod` source (a recorded deviation from the letter of §9.2).** §9.2 says "the member's last vote `date`". The only per-member date available without opening the member's own vote file is T1.6's `latest_vote.date` in the precomputed delegation files, which is the newest **decisive bill** vote. Reading the newest row of every `member_votes/{id}.json` instead would parse 161 MB on each sitemap request. The decisive-vote date is used because it is the date of the page's indexable content: the "Latest final vote" line, the eight "Recent votes" (decision B: decisive votes only), the title and the description all change only when a decisive vote lands. A procedural roll call adds one row deep in the record list. A member with no decisive bill vote (the fixture's G000555) gets no `<lastmod>` rather than an invented one; a `lastmod` that is older than the newest procedural row only makes a crawler less eager, never wrong about content that changed.

   - Next to `from app.routers.bills import VALID_BILL_TYPES` (T7.4; `grep -n "VALID_BILL_TYPES" app/main.py`), add `from app.routers.members import BIOGUIDE_PATTERN` unless it is already imported at module level. (T6.3 imports it inside `serve_member`; leave that local import alone.)

   - Replace the `_inject_meta` block (`grep -n "_title_re = \|def _inject_meta" app/main.py`; baseline lines 54–82, from `_title_re = ...` through `return html.replace("</head>", block + "</head>", 1)`) with:
   ```python
   _title_re = re.compile(r"<title>.*?</title>", re.DOTALL)
   _description_re = re.compile(r'<meta\s+name="description"[^>]*>', re.IGNORECASE)
   _h1_re = re.compile(r"(<h1\b[^>]*>).*?(</h1>)", re.DOTALL)

   _TITLE_SUFFIX = " | ClearVoting"
   _OG_TITLE_MAX = 90
   _ISO_DAY_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")


   def _og_title(title: str) -> str:
       """og:title = the page title without ' | ClearVoting', at most 90 characters (§9.2).

       render.cut_words(text, n) can return n + 1 characters (the '…'), so the cut is at 89.
       """
       base = title.removesuffix(_TITLE_SUFFIX)
       return base if len(base) <= _OG_TITLE_MAX else cut_words(base, _OG_TITLE_MAX - 1)


   def _normalize_bill_params(congress, bill_type, number) -> tuple[int, str, int] | None:
       """(congress, lower-case type, number) by the rule T7.4's serve_bill applies, or None.

       Used by the sitemap so every bill URL it lists is one serve_bill answers with a 200.
       """
       congress_raw = str(congress if congress is not None else "").strip()
       number_raw = str(number if number is not None else "").strip()
       type_lower = str(bill_type or "").strip().lower()
       if not (congress_raw.isdigit() and number_raw.isdigit()) or type_lower not in VALID_BILL_TYPES:
           return None
       congress_int, number_int = int(congress_raw), int(number_raw)
       if not 1 <= congress_int <= 200 or number_int < 1:
           return None
       return congress_int, type_lower, number_int


   def _iso_day(value) -> str | None:
       day = str(value or "")[:10]
       return day if _ISO_DAY_RE.match(day) else None


   def _inject_meta(html: str, meta: dict) -> str:
       """Replace the page <title> and inject SEO/social meta tags before </head>.

       Strips any static <meta name="description"> so the dynamic one isn't duplicated.
       Optional keys: og_type, og_title, image {path, width, height, alt},
       canonical (False omits the canonical link and og:url), h1 (replaces the
       text of the shell's first <h1>). Runs before content is injected, so h1
       only ever touches the shell's own heading.
       """
       title = escape(meta["title"])
       html = _title_re.sub(lambda _m: f"<title>{title}</title>", html, count=1)
       html = _description_re.sub("", html, count=1)
       if meta.get("h1"):
           h1_text = escape(meta["h1"])
           html = _h1_re.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{h1_text}{m.group(2)}", html, count=1)

       description = escape(meta["description"])
       og_title = escape(meta.get("og_title") or _og_title(meta["title"]))
       og_type = escape(meta.get("og_type", "website"))
       canonical = meta.get("canonical", meta.get("url"))
       image = meta.get("image")
       tags = [
           f'<meta name="description" content="{description}">',
           f'<meta property="og:title" content="{og_title}">',
           f'<meta property="og:description" content="{description}">',
           f'<meta property="og:type" content="{og_type}">',
       ]
       if canonical:
           tags.append(f'<meta property="og:url" content="{escape(canonical)}">')
       tags.append('<meta property="og:site_name" content="ClearVoting">')
       if image:
           tags += [
               f'<meta property="og:image" content="{escape(SITE_URL + image["path"])}">',
               f'<meta property="og:image:width" content="{int(image.get("width", 1200))}">',
               f'<meta property="og:image:height" content="{int(image.get("height", 630))}">',
               f'<meta property="og:image:alt" content="{escape(image["alt"])}">',
               '<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">',
           ]
       else:
           tags.append('<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">')
       if canonical:
           tags.append(f'<link rel="canonical" href="{escape(canonical)}">')
       block = "\n    " + "\n    ".join(tags) + "\n"
       return html.replace("</head>", block + "</head>", 1)
   ```
   Why `twitter:card` depends on `image`: §9.2 makes the card `summary_large_image`, and a large card with no image renders as a blank box, so the large card is emitted exactly when an image is. Once T8.4 lands every page except the 404 carries an image, which is the spec's end state; if T8.4 is cut, pages keep today's `summary` card.

   def _state_meta(code: str) -> dict:
       """SEO meta for a delegation page (spec §9.2).

       `code` is a covered, upper-case code: T4.2's serve_state has already turned anything
       else into a 404. district and zip are additive params, so the canonical is always
       /state?code=XX.
       """
       from app.dependencies import get_data_service
       state_name = render.COVERED_STATE_NAMES[code]
       count = len(get_data_service().get_members_by_state(code)["members"])
       return {
           "title": f"{state_name}'s Representatives — Voting Records{_TITLE_SUFFIX}",
           "description": (
               f"Voting records for {count} members of Congress from {state_name}. "
               "See how they vote on bills — facts only, no opinions."
           ),
           "url": f"{SITE_URL}/state?code={code}",
       }


   def _zip_finder_meta() -> dict:
       """Meta for /state pages without a code (empty form, malformed ZIP, ZIP not found).

       These answer one visitor's query and are not pages to index, so no canonical tag.

       return {
           "title": f"Find your representatives{_TITLE_SUFFIX}",
           "description": (
               "Enter your ZIP code to see how your two senators and your House member voted "
               "— facts only, no opinions."
           ),
           "url": f"{SITE_URL}/state",
           "canonical": False,
       }

7. [ ] **Replace the sitemap.** Replace `serve_sitemap` (`grep -n '@app.get("/sitemap.xml")' app/main.py`; baseline lines 264–293, through `return Response(content=xml, media_type="application/xml")`) with:
   ```python
   @app.get("/sitemap.xml")
   def serve_sitemap() -> Response:
       from app.dependencies import get_data_service
       data_service = get_data_service()
       last_sync = _iso_day(data_service.get_sync_metadata().get("last_sync"))

       entries: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = [
           (f"{SITE_URL}/", last_sync),
           (f"{SITE_URL}/about", last_sync),
           (f"{SITE_URL}/methodology", last_sync),
           (f"{SITE_URL}/privacy", None),
       ]

       # State roster date and each member's lastmod come from T1.6's precomputed
       # delegation files (one cached read per state). A member's lastmod is
       # latest_vote.date, the newest decisive bill vote: the date the page's
       # indexable content last changed (see "Member lastmod source" above).
       member_last_vote: dict[str, str | None] = {}
       for code in render.COVERED_STATE_NAMES:
           overview = data_service.get_state_overview(code) or {}
           entries.append((f"{SITE_URL}/state?code={code}", _iso_day(overview.get("roster_as_of"))))
           for member in overview.get("senators", []) + overview.get("house", []):
               bioguide = str(member.get("bioguideId") or "").upper()
               member_last_vote[bioguide] = _iso_day((member.get("latest_vote") or {}).get("date"))

       for member in data_service._members:
           bioguide = str(member.get("bioguideId") or "").strip().upper()
           if BIOGUIDE_PATTERN.match(bioguide):
               entries.append((f"{SITE_URL}/member?id={bioguide}", member_last_vote.get(bioguide)))

       index_bills = (data_service._votes_index or {}).get("bills", {})
       for bill in data_service._bills:
           params = _normalize_bill_params(bill.get("congress"), bill.get("type"), bill.get("number"))
           if params is None:
               continue
           congress, bill_type, number = params
           entry = index_bills.get(f"{congress}-{bill_type}-{number}")
           activity = _iso_day(entry.get("activity_date")) if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
           if activity is None:
               activity = _iso_day((bill.get("latestAction") or {}).get("actionDate"))
           entries.append((f"{SITE_URL}/bill?congress={congress}&type={bill_type}&number={number}", activity))

       def url_tag(loc: str, lastmod: str | None) -> str:
           body = f"<loc>{xml_escape(loc)}</loc>"
           if lastmod:
               body += f"<lastmod>{lastmod}</lastmod>"
           return f"<url>{body}</url>"

       urls = "".join(url_tag(loc, lastmod) for loc, lastmod in entries)
       xml = (
           '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>'
           '<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">'
           f"{urls}</urlset>"
       )
       return Response(content=xml, media_type="application/xml")
   ```
   `/privacy` has no data-derived date, so it carries no `lastmod` rather than a false one; the same holds for a member whose `latest_vote` is null. The `latestAction.actionDate` fallback only applies to a bill missing from the index (every production bill has a roll call, §Dates; some fixture bills do not).

   with:
   ```python
   _COMMIT_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}$")


   def _compute_asset_version(static_root: Path, environ) -> str:
       """Cache-bust token for ?v= links (§9.5).

       RENDER_GIT_COMMIT (first 12 characters) when Render sets it; otherwise a hash
       of the static/ file list with sizes and mtimes, computed once at startup, so an
       idle restart of the same deploy keeps the same ?v= (the old process-start
       timestamp changed it several times a day and defeated the immutable cache).
       """
       commit = str(environ.get("RENDER_GIT_COMMIT") or "").strip()
       if _COMMIT_RE.match(commit):
           return commit[:12].lower()
       digest = hashlib.sha256()
       for path in sorted(p for p in static_root.rglob("*") if p.is_file()):
           stat = path.stat()
           digest.update(f"{path.relative_to(static_root).as_posix()}:{stat.st_size}:{stat.st_mtime_ns}\n".encode())
       return digest.hexdigest()[:12]


   _asset_version = _compute_asset_version(static_dir, os.environ)
   ```
   These lines must sit **after** `static_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "static"` (they do at baseline). Then run `grep -n "time\." app/main.py`; if nothing else uses `time`, delete `import time`. `_version_re` stays `re.compile(r'\?v=\d+')`: the shells on disk keep their digit `?v=N` links (June plan constraint) and the server rewrites them to the 12-character token at serve time.

5. [ ] **Add the rule function.** Directly above `@app.middleware("http")` (`grep -n '@app.middleware("http")' app/main.py`) add:
   ```python
   CACHE_NO_STORE = "no-store"
   CACHE_404 = "public, max-age=60"
   CACHE_STATIC = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
   CACHE_OG = "public, max-age=86400"
   CACHE_FAVICON = "public, max-age=31536000"
   CACHE_HTML = "public, max-age=0, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=3600"
   CACHE_ZIP_REDIRECT = "public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400"
   CACHE_API = "public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400"

   _HTML_ROUTES = frozenset({"/", "/state", "/member", "/bill", "/about", "/methodology", "/privacy"})
   _NO_STORE_ROUTES = frozenset({"/api/health", "/api/notify", "/api/feedback"})
   _REDIRECT_STATUSES = frozenset({301, 302, 303, 307, 308})


   def _cache_control_for(method: str, path: str, query, status: int, existing: str | None) -> str | None:
       """Cache-Control by status first, then by route (spec §9.5).

       Returns the header value to set, or None to leave the response untouched.
       Nothing per-visitor is ever in the HTML (cv-home and the party reveal live in
       the browser), so shells and data are safe to share at the edge.
       """
       if status >= 500 or (400 <= status < 500 and status != 404):
           return CACHE_NO_STORE
       if status == 404:
           return CACHE_404
       if method not in ("GET", "HEAD") or path in _NO_STORE_ROUTES:
           return CACHE_NO_STORE
       if status in _REDIRECT_STATUSES:
           # The ZIP lookup is static per deploy; any other redirect is not cached.
           return CACHE_ZIP_REDIRECT if path == "/state" and "zip" in query else CACHE_NO_STORE
       if status not in (200, 304):
           return existing
       if path.startswith("/static/og/"):
           return CACHE_OG
       if path.startswith("/static/"):
           return CACHE_STATIC
       if path == "/favicon.ico":
           return CACHE_FAVICON
       if path.startswith("/api/"):
           # /api/districts sets its own day-long header (§5.2); keep a route's own value.
           return existing or CACHE_API
       if path in _HTML_ROUTES:
           return CACHE_HTML
       return existing
   ```

5. [ ] **Compute the metric-matched fallbacks.** Create `/Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/fonts/fallback_metrics.py`:
   ```python
   """Print the six metric-matched fallback @font-face rules for static/css/site.css.

   Dev-time only (tools venv: fonttools + brotli). Compares each web font with the
   local face it stands in for during font-display: swap, so the swapped text keeps
   the same width and line height and nothing shifts (spec §9.6, F55).

       venv-og/bin/python fonts/fallback_metrics.py <worktree>/static/fonts
   """
   import sys
   from pathlib import Path

   from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont

   SUPPLEMENTAL = Path("/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental")
   SAMPLE = (
       "The House passed it, 237 to 169, on September 3, 2026. "
       "How did your representatives vote on this bill?"
   )
   # (fallback family, weight, web font file, local fallback file, local() names)
   # One row per weight the site sets, each measured against that weight's web font.
   PAIRS = [
       ("Playfair Display Fallback", 700, "playfair-display-700.woff2", "Georgia Bold.ttf",
        ("Georgia Bold", "Georgia-Bold")),
       ("Lora Fallback", 400, "lora-400.woff2", "Georgia.ttf", ("Georgia",)),
       ("Lora Fallback", 500, "lora-500.woff2", "Georgia.ttf", ("Georgia",)),
       ("Inter Fallback", 400, "inter-400.woff2", "Arial.ttf", ("Arial", "ArialMT")),
       ("Inter Fallback", 600, "inter-600.woff2", "Arial Bold.ttf", ("Arial Bold", "Arial-BoldMT")),
       ("Inter Fallback", 700, "inter-700.woff2", "Arial Bold.ttf", ("Arial Bold", "Arial-BoldMT")),
   ]


   def average_advance(font: TTFont) -> float:
       """Mean advance width of the sample's glyphs, in ems."""
       cmap = font.getBestCmap()
       hmtx = font["hmtx"]
       units = font["head"].unitsPerEm
       widths = [hmtx[cmap[ord(ch)]][0] for ch in SAMPLE if ord(ch) in cmap]
       return sum(widths) / len(widths) / units


   def main(fonts_dir: Path) -> None:
       for family, weight, web_file, local_file, local_names in PAIRS:
           web = TTFont(fonts_dir / web_file)
           fallback = TTFont(SUPPLEMENTAL / local_file)
           size_adjust = average_advance(web) / average_advance(fallback)
           units = web["head"].unitsPerEm
           hhea = web["hhea"]
           src = ", ".join(f'local("{name}")' for name in local_names)
           print("@font-face {")
           print(f'  font-family: "{family}";')
           print(f"  src: {src};")
           print(f"  font-weight: {weight};")
           print(f"  size-adjust: {size_adjust * 100:.2f}%;")
           print(f"  ascent-override: {hhea.ascent / units / size_adjust * 100:.2f}%;")
           print(f"  descent-override: {abs(hhea.descent) / units / size_adjust * 100:.2f}%;")
           print(f"  line-gap-override: {hhea.lineGap / units / size_adjust * 100:.2f}%;")
           print("}")


   if __name__ == "__main__":
       main(Path(sys.argv[1]))
   ```
   Run it:
   ```bash
   /Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/venv-og/bin/python /Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/fonts/fallback_metrics.py /Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/redesign-2026-09/static/fonts
   ```
   Expected: six `@font-face { … }` rules on stdout (Playfair 700, Lora 400, Lora 500, Inter 400, Inter 600, Inter 700), each with four percentages; every `size-adjust` between 85% and 125%. Why these weights: the Playfair fallback is declared at 700 against Georgia Bold because Playfair is only ever set at 600–800 (800 resolves to the 700 face, already bold); Inter 600/700 (kickers, nav, seals, chips, buttons) get Arial Bold faces measured against inter-600/inter-700, so their swap text is a real bold face of matching width instead of a synthetic bold of the 400-metric Arial; Lora 500 gets its own Georgia face measured against lora-500. Inter 500 resolves to the 400 face under the CSS weight-matching rule (for 500 it looks lighter first), which never triggers synthetic bold. Both `Arial Bold.ttf` and `Georgia Bold.ttf` are in `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/` on this Mac.

3. [ ] **Write the card script.** Create `scripts/build_og_cards.py`:
   ```python
   """Build the four Phase A share cards (1200x630) into static/og/ (spec §9.3).

   Dev-time only. Runs with the out-of-repo tools venv (Pillow, fontTools, brotli);
   Pillow is never added to requirements.txt and nothing renders on the request path.

       /Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/tools/venv-og/bin/python scripts/build_og_cards.py
   """
   import io
   from pathlib import Path

   from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
   from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

   ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
   FONTS = ROOT / "static" / "fonts"
   OUT = ROOT / "static" / "og"

   WIDTH, HEIGHT = 1200, 630
   MARGIN = 80

   # §6.1 tokens
   PAPER = "#F5F6FA"
   INK = "#1B1B1B"
   INK_META = "#5F656D"
   NAVY = "#112E51"
   BLUE = "#0071BC"
   BLUE_DIM = "#205493"
   RULE = "#D6D7D9"

   TAGLINE = "Facts only · No opinions · No spin"
   DOMAIN = "clearvoting.org"
   # card name -> one-line descriptor (§9.3); the default card carries the tagline only
   CARDS = {
       "default": None,
       "member": "Voting record",
       "bill": "How Congress voted",
       "state": "Your representatives",
   }


   def load_font(filename: str, size: int) -> ImageFont.FreeTypeFont:
       """Open a committed woff2 face: decompress to TrueType in memory for FreeType."""
       font = TTFont(FONTS / filename)
       font.flavor = None
       buffer = io.BytesIO()
       font.save(buffer)
       buffer.seek(0)
       return ImageFont.truetype(buffer, size)


   def double_rule(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, y: int) -> None:
       """The masthead's 3px + 1px navy double rule across the margins."""
       draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, WIDTH - MARGIN, y + 2], fill=NAVY)
       draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y + 6, WIDTH - MARGIN, y + 6], fill=NAVY)


   def draw_tracked_centered(draw, y, text, font, fill, tracking) -> None:
       """Centre `text` on the card with extra letter spacing (kicker style)."""
       widths = [draw.textlength(ch, font=font) for ch in text]
       x = (WIDTH - (sum(widths) + tracking * (len(text) - 1))) / 2
       for ch, width in zip(text, widths):
           draw.text((x, y), ch, font=font, fill=fill, anchor="ls")
           x += width + tracking


   def build_card(descriptor: str | None) -> Image.Image:
       image = Image.new("RGB", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), PAPER)
       draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)

       double_rule(draw, 72)

       # Wordmark: "Clear" Playfair 800 navy + "Voting" Playfair 600 italic blue, one baseline.
       clear_font = load_font("playfair-display-800.woff2", 128)
       voting_font = load_font("playfair-display-600-italic.woff2", 128)
       clear_width = draw.textlength("Clear", font=clear_font)
       voting_width = draw.textlength("Voting", font=voting_font)
       x = (WIDTH - (clear_width + voting_width)) / 2
       draw.text((x, 236), "Clear", font=clear_font, fill=NAVY, anchor="ls")
       draw.text((x + clear_width, 236), "Voting", font=voting_font, fill=BLUE, anchor="ls")

       draw_tracked_centered(draw, 292, TAGLINE.upper(), load_font("inter-700.woff2", 24), INK_META, 3.4)

       draw.rectangle([MARGIN, 336, WIDTH - MARGIN, 336], fill=RULE)

       if descriptor:
           draw.text((WIDTH / 2, 456), descriptor, font=load_font("playfair-display-700.woff2", 76),
                     fill=INK, anchor="ms")

       draw.text((WIDTH / 2, 536), DOMAIN, font=load_font("inter-600.woff2", 30), fill=BLUE_DIM, anchor="ms")
       double_rule(draw, 556)
       return image


   def main() -> None:
       OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
       for name, descriptor in CARDS.items():
           path = OUT / f"{name}.png"
           build_card(descriptor).save(path, optimize=True)
           print(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}  {path.stat().st_size // 1024} KB")


   if __name__ == "__main__":
       main()
   ```

Read a PNG only when the text offender list does not explain a `fold` or `scroll` failure.

   ```js
   // gates.mjs — ClearVoting redesign §6.9 definition-of-done browser gates, items 1–6 and 8.
   // Usage: node gates.mjs [baseUrl] [outdir] [--only=page,page] [--shots]
   //    or: node gates.mjs [outdir] name=http://… [name=http://…]   (shoot.mjs-style ad-hoc pages; only these run;
   //        names starting "404" expect HTTP 404; fold target by path: / → Find button, /member → first .vote-row,
   //        /bill → "How did your representatives vote?", none on 404s or ?page= record pages)
   //   baseUrl defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8011; outdir defaults to ./gates-out next to this file.
   //   --only filters by PAGE NAME (e.g. --only=home,404), not by check name.
   //   Prints one FAIL line per failing check plus a per-check summary, writes <outdir>/gates.json,
   //   exits 1 when any gated check fails. Lives out of the repo on purpose: never run in pytest or CI.
   import { chromium } from 'playwright';
   import { mkdirSync, existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
   import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
   import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
   import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

   const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
   const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
   const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
   const flags = Object.fromEntries(
     argv.filter((a) => a.startsWith('--')).map((a) => {
       const [k, v] = a.slice(2).split('=');
       return [k, v ?? true];
     }),
   );
   const positional = argv.filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
   // shoot.mjs-style ad-hoc pages (name=http://…), the form T10.2/T10.4/T10.5 call this runner with.
   const PAIRS = positional.filter((a) => /^[\w.-]+=https?:\/\//.test(a));
   const rest = positional.filter((a) => !PAIRS.includes(a));
   // With pairs, the only other positional (if any) is the outdir; without pairs it is [baseUrl] [outdir].
   const [baseArg, outArg] = PAIRS.length ? [undefined, rest[0]] : rest;
   const firstPairOrigin = PAIRS.length ? new URL(PAIRS[0].slice(PAIRS[0].indexOf('=') + 1)).origin : null;
   const BASE = (baseArg || firstPairOrigin || 'http://127.0.0.1:8011').replace(/\/$/, '');
   const OUT = outArg || join(HERE, 'gates-out');
   const ONLY = flags.only ? new Set(String(flags.only).split(',')) : null;
   const SHOTS = Boolean(flags.shots);
   const MAX_SHOTS = 6;
   const SITE_CSS = '/Users/josephgarcia/.clearvote-worktrees/redesign-2026-09/static/css/site.css';
   const AXE_SRC = readFileSync(require.resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js'), 'utf8');
   const ON_DISK = '/Users/josephgarcia/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1223/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell';
   const LAUNCH = existsSync(ON_DISK) ? { executablePath: ON_DISK } : {};
   mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });

   // Member photos come from www.congress.gov. A 403/404/flake there is a normal state the initials fallback
   // handles (§6.3), not a build defect, so every context serves a 1x1 PNG for them: runs are deterministic
   // and work offline. The URL is unchanged, so the CSP img-src rule is still exercised.
   const PHOTO_ROUTE = 'https://www.congress.gov/img/**';
   const PIXEL = Buffer.from('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mNkYAAAAAYAAjCB0C8AAAAASUVORK5CYII=', 'base64');
   const stubPhoto = (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: 'image/png', body: PIXEL });

   // A returning visitor (spec §5.4 key shape). Pages marked home:true get it before any script runs.
   const CV_HOME = JSON.stringify({ state: 'NY', district: 4, savedAt: '2026-09-22' });

   const FIND_BUTTON = { edge: 'bottom', tags: 'button', text: 'Find my representatives', max: 600 };
   const FIRST_VOTE_ROW = { edge: 'top', selector: '.vote-row', max: 812 };
   const REPS_HEADING = { edge: 'top', tags: 'h2', text: 'How did your representatives vote?', max: 812 };
   // §4.1 desktop: both lead columns finish within ≈700px, so The Record head is on the first 1280x800 screen
   // (T3.3's v0 check, kept). First visit only: a remembered visitor's module 4 sits above the Record by design.
   const RECORD_HEAD = { edge: 'top', selector: '#record-h', max: 800 };

   // Every template (index, state, member, bill, about, methodology, privacy, 404) plus the §6.9 #6 fold fixtures.
   const DEFAULT_PAGES = [
     { name: 'home', path: '/', fold: FIND_BUTTON, foldDesktop: RECORD_HEAD },
     { name: 'home-remembered', path: '/', home: true, fold: FIND_BUTTON },
     { name: 'state-ny', path: '/state?code=NY' },
     { name: 'state-ny-d4', path: '/state?code=NY&district=4' },
     { name: 'state-ca', path: '/state?code=CA' },
     { name: 'zip-split', path: '/state?zip=11201' },
     { name: 'zip-partial', path: '/state?zip=73949' },
     { name: 'zip-none', path: '/state?zip=44101' },
     { name: 'member-s000148', path: '/member?id=S000148', fold: FIRST_VOTE_ROW },
     { name: 'member-s000148-remembered', path: '/member?id=S000148', home: true, fold: FIRST_VOTE_ROW },
     { name: 'member-g000602', path: '/member?id=G000602', fold: FIRST_VOTE_ROW },
     { name: 'member-party', path: '/member?id=S000148&show_party=true' },
     { name: 'bill-119-hr-4795', path: '/bill?congress=119&type=hr&number=4795', fold: REPS_HEADING },
     { name: 'bill-119-hr-4795-remembered', path: '/bill?congress=119&type=hr&number=4795', home: true, fold: REPS_HEADING },
     { name: 'bill-119-hres-1499', path: '/bill?congress=119&type=hres&number=1499', fold: REPS_HEADING },
     { name: 'bill-119-hres-354', path: '/bill?congress=119&type=hres&number=354', fold: REPS_HEADING },
     { name: 'bill-118-hr-21', path: '/bill?congress=118&type=hr&number=21' },
     { name: 'about', path: '/about' },
     { name: 'methodology', path: '/methodology' },
     { name: 'privacy', path: '/privacy' },
     { name: '404', path: '/no-such-page-in-this-edition', status: 404 },
   ];

   // Ad-hoc page from a name=url pair. §6.9 #6 fold targets apply to a template's first screen, so they are
   // attached by path and skipped on 404s and on ?page= record pages.
   const FOLD_BY_PATH = { '/': FIND_BUTTON, '/member': FIRST_VOTE_ROW, '/bill': REPS_HEADING };
   function adHocPage(pair) {
     const i = pair.indexOf('=');
     const name = pair.slice(0, i);
     const url = pair.slice(i + 1);
     const u = new URL(url);
     const is404 = name.startsWith('404');
     const fold = is404 || u.searchParams.has('page') ? null : FOLD_BY_PATH[u.pathname] || null;
     return { name, url, status: is404 ? 404 : 200, fold };
   }
   const PAGES = (PAIRS.length ? PAIRS.map(adHocPage) : DEFAULT_PAGES).filter((p) => !ONLY || ONLY.has(p.name));
   const urlOf = (p) => p.url || BASE + p.path;
   // The §6.4 dialog check runs on one page per template; the JS-off pass on the four spine fixtures.
   // In pair mode both run on the pair pages (the JS-off pass only on those with a fold target).
   const DIALOG_NAMES = new Set(['home', 'state-ny', 'member-s000148', 'bill-119-hr-4795', 'about', 'methodology', 'privacy', '404']);
   const NOJS_NAMES = new Set(['home', 'state-ny', 'member-s000148', 'bill-119-hr-4795']);
   const DIALOG_PAGES = PAIRS.length ? PAGES : PAGES.filter((p) => DIALOG_NAMES.has(p.name));
   const NOJS_PAGES = PAIRS.length ? PAGES.filter((p) => p.fold) : PAGES.filter((p) => NOJS_NAMES.has(p.name));

   const VIEWPORTS = [[320, 640], [375, 812], [768, 1024], [1280, 800]];
   const AXE_VIEWPORTS = [[375, 812], [1280, 800]];
   const AXE_TAGS = ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa', 'best-practice'];
   // §6.9 #8: contrast, name/role, heading-order and landmark rules are gated; every other axe finding is informational.
   const AXE_GATED = new Set([
     'color-contrast',
     'heading-order', 'page-has-heading-one', 'empty-heading',
     'region', 'bypass',
     'button-name', 'link-name', 'input-button-name', 'select-name', 'label', 'label-content-name-mismatch',
     'image-alt', 'role-img-alt', 'svg-img-alt',
     'aria-roles', 'aria-allowed-role', 'aria-required-attr', 'aria-required-children', 'aria-required-parent',
     'aria-valid-attr', 'aria-valid-attr-value', 'aria-command-name', 'aria-input-field-name',
     'aria-toggle-field-name', 'aria-dialog-name', 'aria-meter-name', 'aria-progressbar-name', 'aria-tooltip-name',
     'list', 'listitem', 'definition-list', 'dlitem', 'document-title', 'html-has-lang',
   ]);
   const axeGated = (id) => AXE_GATED.has(id) || id.startsWith('landmark-');

   // §6.1 token values, verbatim.
   const SPEC_TOKENS = {
     '--paper': '#F5F6FA', '--card': '#FFFFFF', '--ink': '#1B1B1B', '--ink-soft': '#5B616B',
     '--ink-meta': '#5F656D', '--navy': '#112E51', '--blue': '#0071BC', '--blue-dim': '#205493',
     '--yes': '#2E7D3A', '--yes-text': '#1F5E2D', '--yes-tint': '#DDE7E3', '--no': '#B3261E',
     '--no-text': '#8E1B21', '--no-tint': '#EDDDE0', '--error': '#8A1C1C', '--rule': '#D6D7D9',
     '--rule-soft': '#E8E8E8', '--tap': '44px', '--radius-chip': '4px', '--radius-ctl': '8px',
   };
   const TEXT_TOKENS = ['--ink', '--ink-soft', '--ink-meta', '--navy', '--blue', '--blue-dim', '--yes', '--yes-text', '--no', '--no-text', '--error'];
   const EXTRA_PAIRS = [['--yes-text', '--yes-tint'], ['--no-text', '--no-tint'], ['--card', '--navy']];

   const results = [];
   const axeInfo = [];
   const record = (check, page, width, ok, detail, offenders = []) => {
     results.push({ check, page, width, ok, detail, offenders: offenders.slice(0, 10) });
   };

   function channel(c) {
     const s = c / 255;
     return s <= 0.03928 ? s / 12.92 : ((s + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
   }
   function luminance(hex) {
     let h = hex.replace('#', '').trim();
     if (h.length === 3) h = h.split('').map((x) => x + x).join('');
     const [r, g, b] = [0, 2, 4].map((i) => channel(parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16)));
     return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b;
   }
   function contrast(a, b) {
     const [hi, lo] = [luminance(a), luminance(b)].sort((x, y) => y - x);
     return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05);
   }

   // §6.9 #3: recompute every text token's contrast from site.css :root (no browser needed).
   function checkTokens() {
     const css = readFileSync(SITE_CSS, 'utf8');
     const root = css.match(/:root\s*\{([^}]*)\}/);
     if (!root) {
       record('tokens', 'site.css', null, false, 'no :root block found in site.css');
       return;
     }
     const tokens = {};
     for (const [, key, value] of root[1].matchAll(/(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);/g)) tokens[key] = value.trim();
     for (const [key, want] of Object.entries(SPEC_TOKENS)) {
       const have = tokens[key];
       record('tokens', 'site.css', null, (have || '').toLowerCase() === want.toLowerCase(), `${key} is ${have ?? 'missing'}; spec §6.1 says ${want}`);
     }
     const pairs = [];
     for (const t of TEXT_TOKENS) for (const ground of ['--paper', '--card']) pairs.push([t, ground]);
     pairs.push(...EXTRA_PAIRS);
     for (const [fg, bg] of pairs) {
       if (!/^#[0-9a-f]{3,6}$/i.test(tokens[fg] || '') || !/^#[0-9a-f]{3,6}$/i.test(tokens[bg] || '')) {
         record('contrast', 'site.css', null, false, `${fg} on ${bg}: token missing or not a hex colour`);
         continue;
       }
       const ratio = contrast(tokens[fg], tokens[bg]);
       record('contrast', 'site.css', null, ratio >= 4.5, `${fg} on ${bg} = ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1 (needs 4.5:1)`);
     }
     const bytes = statSync(SITE_CSS).size;
     console.log(`info site.css is ${bytes} bytes (target <= 30720, spec §6.7)`);
   }

   // Runs inside the page. Self-contained: Playwright serialises this function's source.
   function domChecks({ fold, narrow }) {
     const norm = (s) => (s || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
     const describe = (el) => {
       let s = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
       if (el.id) s += `#${el.id}`;
       if (el.classList && el.classList.length) s += `.${[...el.classList].join('.')}`;
       const text = norm(el.textContent).slice(0, 40);
       return text ? `${s} "${text}"` : s;
     };
     const visible = (el) => {
       if (!el.getClientRects().length) return false;
       const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
       return cs.visibility !== 'hidden' && cs.display !== 'none';
     };
     window.scrollTo(0, 0);
     const all = [...document.querySelectorAll('body *')];
     const out = {};

     // §6.9 #1 reflow.
     const sw = document.documentElement.scrollWidth;
     const iw = window.innerWidth;
     const wide = [];
     if (sw > iw) {
       for (const el of all) {
         if (wide.length >= 10) break;
         const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
         if (r.right > iw + 0.5 && visible(el)) wide.push(`${describe(el)} right=${Math.round(r.right)}`);
       }
     }
     out.scroll = { ok: sw <= iw, detail: `scrollWidth=${sw} innerWidth=${iw}`, offenders: wide };

     // §6.9 #2 no rendered text under 12px.
     const small = [];
     const seen = new Set();
     const walker = document.createTreeWalker(document.body, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
     while (walker.nextNode()) {
       const node = walker.currentNode;
       const el = node.parentElement;
       if (!el || seen.has(el) || !node.textContent.trim()) continue;
       seen.add(el);
       if (el.closest('script, style, noscript, template') || !visible(el)) continue;
       const px = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize);
       if (px < 12) small.push(`${describe(el)} ${px}px`);
     }
     out.fonts = { ok: small.length === 0, detail: `${small.length} text elements under 12px`, offenders: small };

     // §6.9 #4 target size: every standalone control (the listed selectors and every other visible a[href])
     // needs 44x44. Exempt, per the spec's WCAG 2.5.8 inline exception: an <a> inside running text — a p/li/dd
     // whose text outside its links and buttons contains words (so the footer data line's Congress.gov and
     // Senate.gov links are exempt, while a p.actions row of bare links is not) — and tabindex=-1 focus
     // targets. The controls §6.9 #4 names by their text ("Change", "Forget", …) need 44 even inside a line.
     // The inline test runs before the selector list, so a sentence link is exempt even if a selector matches it.
     const REQUIRED = [
       'button', 'input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=hidden])', 'select', 'textarea', 'summary',
       '.vote-row', '.person', '.bill-row', '.state-link', '.btn', '.btn--secondary', '.party-toggle',
       '.masthead-nav a', '.footer-links a', '.site-footer button', '.actions a', '.actions button',
     ].join(', ');
     const NAMED = /^(Change|Change ZIP|Forget|This is my district →?|Remember .+|Roll call source →|← .+|Older votes →)$/;
     const inRunningText = (el) => {
       const block = el.closest('p, li, dd');
       if (!block) return false;
       const copy = block.cloneNode(true);
       for (const c of copy.querySelectorAll('a, button')) c.remove();
       return /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(copy.textContent);
     };
     const tiny = [];
     for (const el of new Set([...document.querySelectorAll(`${REQUIRED}, a[href]`)])) {
       if (!visible(el) || el.getAttribute('tabindex') === '-1') continue;
       const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
       if (r.bottom <= 0 || r.right <= 0 || (r.width <= 1 && r.height <= 1)) continue; // parked skip link / visually hidden
       const named = NAMED.test(norm(el.textContent));
       const exempt = !named && el.tagName === 'A' && inRunningText(el);
       const min = exempt ? 0 : 43.5;
       if (r.width < min || r.height < min) tiny.push(`${describe(el)} ${Math.round(r.width)}x${Math.round(r.height)} (needs 44)`);
     }
     for (const label of document.querySelectorAll('label')) {
       if (!label.querySelector('input[type=checkbox]') || !visible(label)) continue;
       const h = label.getBoundingClientRect().height;
       if (h < 43.5) tiny.push(`${describe(label)} checkbox row ${Math.round(h)}px (needs 44)`);
     }
     out.targets = { ok: tiny.length === 0, detail: `${tiny.length} undersized targets`, offenders: tiny };

     // §6.9 #5 box-shadow only on .state-link/.vote-card; radii only 0/4px/8px (elements and their ::before/::after).
     const OK_RADII = new Set(['0px', '4px', '8px']);
     const CORNERS = ['borderTopLeftRadius', 'borderTopRightRadius', 'borderBottomRightRadius', 'borderBottomLeftRadius'];
     const decor = [];
     for (const el of all) {
       if (!visible(el)) continue;
       for (const pseudo of [null, '::before', '::after']) {
         const cs = getComputedStyle(el, pseudo);
         if (pseudo && (cs.content === 'none' || cs.content === 'normal')) continue;
         const where = describe(el) + (pseudo || '');
         if (cs.boxShadow !== 'none' && !(pseudo === null && el.matches('.state-link, .vote-card'))) decor.push(`box-shadow ${cs.boxShadow} on ${where}`);
         const bad = CORNERS.map((c) => cs[c]).find((v) => !v.split(' ').every((part) => OK_RADII.has(part)));
         if (bad) decor.push(`border-radius ${bad} on ${where}`);
       }
     }
     out.decor = { ok: decor.length === 0, detail: `${decor.length} shadow/radius violations`, offenders: decor };

     // Nothing floats over the primary action on phones: no visible position:fixed element under 880.
     if (narrow) {
       const floating = all.filter((el) => el.tagName !== 'DIALOG' && getComputedStyle(el).position === 'fixed' && visible(el)).map(describe);
       out.floating = { ok: floating.length === 0, detail: `${floating.length} fixed elements under 880px`, offenders: floating };
     }

     // §6.9 #6 fold checks (375x812; plus home's Record head at 1280x800). The caller passes fold only there.
     if (fold) {
       const node = fold.selector
         ? document.querySelector(fold.selector)
         : [...document.querySelectorAll(fold.tags)].find((n) => norm(n.textContent) === fold.text) || null;
       if (!node) {
         out.fold = { ok: false, detail: `${fold.selector || fold.text}: element not found`, offenders: [] };
       } else {
         const r = node.getBoundingClientRect();
         const y = Math.round((fold.edge === 'bottom' ? r.bottom : r.top) + window.scrollY);
         out.fold = { ok: y < fold.max, detail: `${fold.selector || fold.text} ${fold.edge}=${y}px (must be < ${fold.max}px)`, offenders: [] };
       }
     }
     return out;
   }

   async function openPage(ctx, p) {
     const page = await ctx.newPage();
     if (p.home) await page.addInitScript((value) => localStorage.setItem('cv-home', value), CV_HOME);
     return page;
   }

   async function layoutPass(browser) {
     let shots = 0;
     for (const [width, height] of VIEWPORTS) {
       // CSP stays enforced here so the page renders exactly as it will in production.
       const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height }, deviceScaleFactor: 1, reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
       await ctx.route(PHOTO_ROUTE, stubPhoto);
       for (const p of PAGES) {
         const page = await openPage(ctx, p);
         const errors = [];
         const url = urlOf(p);
         page.on('console', (m) => {
           if (m.type() !== 'error') return;
           if (p.status === 404 && m.location().url === url) return; // the 404 document itself
           errors.push(m.text());
         });
         page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(String(e)));
         let resp;
         try {
           resp = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout: 45000 });
           await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready.then(() => true));
         } catch (e) {
           record('load', p.name, width, false, String(e).slice(0, 160));
           await page.close();
           continue;
         }
         const before = results.filter((r) => !r.ok).length;
         const want = p.status || 200;
         record('status', p.name, width, resp.status() === want, `HTTP ${resp.status()} (want ${want})`);
         const fold = width === 375 ? p.fold || null : width === 1280 ? p.foldDesktop || null : null;
         const dom = await page.evaluate(domChecks, { fold, narrow: width < 880 });
         for (const [check, r] of Object.entries(dom)) record(check, p.name, width, r.ok, r.detail, r.offenders);
         record('console', p.name, width, errors.length === 0, `${errors.length} console errors`, errors);
         if (SHOTS && shots < MAX_SHOTS && results.filter((r) => !r.ok).length > before) {
           await page.screenshot({ path: join(OUT, `${p.name}-${width}.png`) });
           shots += 1;
         }
         await page.close();
       }
       await ctx.close();
     }
   }

   async function axePass(browser) {
     for (const [width, height] of AXE_VIEWPORTS) {
       // bypassCSP only so the axe source can be injected; layout checks above run with CSP on.
       const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height }, deviceScaleFactor: 1, reducedMotion: 'reduce', bypassCSP: true });
       await ctx.route(PHOTO_ROUTE, stubPhoto);
       for (const p of PAGES) {
         const page = await openPage(ctx, p);
         try {
           await page.goto(urlOf(p), { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout: 45000 });
           await page.addScriptTag({ content: AXE_SRC });
           const violations = await page.evaluate(async (tags) => {
             const res = await window.axe.run(document, { resultTypes: ['violations'], runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: tags } });
             return res.violations.map((v) => ({ id: v.id, count: v.nodes.length, nodes: v.nodes.slice(0, 5).map((n) => n.target.join(' ')) }));
           }, AXE_TAGS);
           const gated = violations.filter((v) => axeGated(v.id));
           for (const v of violations.filter((x) => !axeGated(x.id))) axeInfo.push({ page: p.name, width, id: v.id, count: v.count });
           record('axe', p.name, width, gated.length === 0, `${gated.length} gated axe rules violated`, gated.map((v) => `${v.id} x${v.count}: ${v.nodes.join(' | ')}`));
         } catch (e) {
           record('axe', p.name, width, false, `axe run failed: ${String(e).slice(0, 160)}`);
         }
         await page.close();
       }
       await ctx.close();
     }
   }

   // T2.4's §6.4 dialog check, carried over to the rewritten shells: keyboard open from the footer button →
   // focus in the textarea; success copy stays in the dialog; failure copy; Esc closes and focus returns to
   // the opener. /api/feedback is stubbed, so nothing reaches the feedback sheet. Where a page carries a
   // feedback hook (.state-header h1, .member-header h1, .bill-header h1) the context line must be filled.
   async function dialogPass(browser) {
     const SENT = 'Thanks — sent.';
     const FAILED = "We couldn't send that. Please try again in a few minutes.";
     for (const [width, height] of [[375, 812], [1280, 800]]) {
       const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height }, deviceScaleFactor: 1, reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
       await ctx.route(PHOTO_ROUTE, stubPhoto);
       for (const p of DIALOG_PAGES) {
         const page = await openPage(ctx, p);
         let failNext = false;
         await page.route('**/api/feedback', (route) => route.fulfill(failNext
           ? { status: 500, contentType: 'application/json', body: '{"detail":"stubbed failure"}' }
           : { status: 200, contentType: 'application/json', body: '{"status":"ok"}' }));
         try {
           await page.goto(urlOf(p), { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout: 45000 });
           await page.focus('#feedback-open');
           await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
           const opened = await page.evaluate(() => ({
             open: document.getElementById('feedback-modal').open,
             focus: document.activeElement ? document.activeElement.id : '',
             context: document.getElementById('feedback-context').textContent,
             hook: Boolean(document.querySelector('.state-header h1, .member-header h1, .bill-header h1')),
           }));
           await page.fill('#feedback-message', 'gates.mjs dialog check');
           await page.click('#feedback-submit');
           await page.waitForFunction((s) => document.getElementById('feedback-status').textContent === s, SENT, { timeout: 5000 });
           const stillOpen = await page.evaluate(() => document.getElementById('feedback-modal').open);
           failNext = true;
           await page.fill('#feedback-message', 'gates.mjs failure check');
           await page.click('#feedback-submit');
           await page.waitForFunction((s) => document.getElementById('feedback-status').textContent === s, FAILED, { timeout: 5000 });
           await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
           const closed = await page.evaluate(() => ({
             open: document.getElementById('feedback-modal').open,
             focus: document.activeElement ? document.activeElement.id : '',
           }));
           const ok = opened.open && opened.focus === 'feedback-message' && (!opened.hook || opened.context.startsWith('About: '))
             && stillOpen && !closed.open && closed.focus === 'feedback-open';
           record('dialog', p.name, width, ok, `open=${opened.open} focus=${opened.focus} context="${opened.context}" stayedOpen=${stillOpen} closed=${!closed.open} focusBack=${closed.focus}`);
         } catch (e) {
           record('dialog', p.name, width, false, String(e).slice(0, 160));
         }
         await page.close();
       }
       await ctx.close();
     }
   }

   // T3.3's JS-off pass, carried over: the server-rendered page alone must reflow at 375 and meet its fold.
   async function nojsPass(browser) {
     const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 375, height: 812 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1, reducedMotion: 'reduce', javaScriptEnabled: false });
     await ctx.route(PHOTO_ROUTE, stubPhoto);
     for (const p of NOJS_PAGES) {
       const page = await ctx.newPage();
       const name = `${p.name}-nojs`;
       try {
         const resp = await page.goto(urlOf(p), { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout: 45000 });
         const want = p.status || 200;
         record('status', name, 375, resp.status() === want, `HTTP ${resp.status()} (want ${want})`);
         const dom = await page.evaluate(domChecks, { fold: p.fold || null, narrow: true });
         record('scroll', name, 375, dom.scroll.ok, dom.scroll.detail, dom.scroll.offenders);
         if (dom.fold) record('fold', name, 375, dom.fold.ok, dom.fold.detail, dom.fold.offenders);
       } catch (e) {
         record('load', name, 375, false, String(e).slice(0, 160));
       }
       await page.close();
     }
     await ctx.close();
   }

   checkTokens();
   const browser = await chromium.launch(LAUNCH);
   await layoutPass(browser);
   await axePass(browser);
   await dialogPass(browser);
   await nojsPass(browser);
   await browser.close();

   const failed = results.filter((r) => !r.ok);
   for (const f of failed) {
     console.log(`FAIL ${f.check} ${f.page}@${f.width ?? '-'}: ${f.detail}`);
     for (const o of f.offenders) console.log(`     ${o}`);
   }
   const checks = [...new Set(results.map((r) => r.check))];
   for (const c of checks) {
     const rows = results.filter((r) => r.check === c);
     console.log(`${c.padEnd(9)} ${rows.filter((r) => r.ok).length}/${rows.length} pass`);
   }
   if (axeInfo.length) console.log(`info ${axeInfo.length} non-gated axe findings listed in gates.json axe_info`);
   writeFileSync(join(OUT, 'gates.json'), JSON.stringify({ base: BASE, ran_at: new Date().toISOString(), results, axe_info: axeInfo }, null, 1));
   console.log(failed.length ? `GATES FAILED: ${failed.length} failing checks` : 'GATES PASSED');
   process.exit(failed.length ? 1 : 0);
   ```

   Then replace T8.4's `_og_image` **in place** (the same name, in the same spot below `_OG_CARD_ALT`; there must be exactly one `def _og_image` afterwards) with:
   ```python
   def _og_image(kind: str, key: str | None = None, alt: str | None = None) -> dict:
       """The share card for a page (spec §9.3), as the `image` key _inject_meta reads.

       Phase B: the entity's own card (static/og/{kind}/{key}.png) when the startup scan found
       it, described by `alt`; otherwise the Phase A template card static/og/{kind}.png.
       `path` stays site-relative; _inject_meta makes it absolute.
       """
       if key and f"{kind}/{key}.png" in _og_entities:
           return {"path": f"/static/og/{kind}/{key}.png", "width": 1200, "height": 630,
                   "alt": alt or _OG_CARD_ALT[kind]}
       return {"path": f"/static/og/{kind}.png", "width": 1200, "height": 630, "alt": _OG_CARD_ALT[kind]}
   ```
   The membership check means a key can never name a file outside the scanned set. Callers that pass only `kind` get exactly T8.4's dict, so `_bill_meta`, `_zip_finder_meta` and the four static routes are not touched: bill cards stay static (§9.3).
